title: Windows: wire_post tests share one temp file and fail with Access is denied

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: on Windows, `no_skims_is_the_rough_program_and_json_unchanged` in `crates/app/tests/wire_post.rs` can fail. Host `winnie`, main `f0bdc5109`:

```
panicked at crates\app\tests\wire_post.rs:330:63:
the wire program posts: "cannot write C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp\camcraft-wire-skims-7908.nc: Access is denied. (os error 5)"
```

Cause: `post_text()` (line 329) writes to `camcraft-wire-skims-<process id>.nc`. Several tests call it, and they run in parallel threads of one process, so they use the same path. Windows refuses a write while another thread holds or deletes the file. macOS and Linux permit it, so the test passes there.

Fix: give each call its own file (a `tempfile` directory). The other temp names in this file are used by one test each.

Done means: `post_text()` uses a unique path for each call, and `wire_post` passes on Windows.

title: Path kernel K7a: measure the kernel laws on a finished toolpath, and pin the readings of the old planners

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #4023 and of K7 (#4027). It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**). It does not depend on the crate skeleton (#4055, PR #4123): it measures a finished toolpath, so it reads only the toolpath, the region and the stock.

## Why

The switch-over proof of the record `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` needs each law of #4023 "measured on the disc, the dog bone and `fig8.step`, old against new". The measuring code and the readings of the OLD planners can be made now. The K7 suite then runs the same measures on the new planners.

## What to do

1. Add one measuring module for tests (in the existing test helpers of `camcraft-motion`, next to `shape_mask`). For a generated toolpath it gives these readings, each as a number with the list of the places:
   - lifts on one level, and for each lift whether a named reason is given;
   - planar feeds that cross a planned cut or leave the region (a crossing);
   - entries into material: each entry with its kind, and whether it starts in air, in a hole, in a cleared column, or in solid material;
   - cuts above the engagement limit (the radial engagement against the stock that is left), with the worst value;
   - fallbacks: each note that says that a different plan was used.
2. Add a readings test for each phase-1 kind on the three parts where the kind applies, with Inside and Outside where the kind has a start side. The test pins the readings of the OLD planner as they are today (a table in the test, not a pass/fail law). A reading that breaks a law is not a failure of this issue: it is the fact that the kernel must improve. Mark each such reading in the table.
3. Use `fig8.step` only (the tracked public fixture). Never read the private project files in `testdata/models/`.
4. Keep each test under the 60 s debug budget, or use the heavy lane with a light twin by the rules.

## Done means

The measuring module has unit tests on hand-made toolpaths with known readings. The readings table of the old planners is in the PR body, kind by kind, and is pinned by tests on the side branch. No planner code changes.

title: LinuxCNC and Tormach posts write G64 P0 when a blend or smoothing tolerance rounds to zero

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: the LinuxCNC and Tormach posts write `G64 P0` when a blend or smoothing tolerance is under the written resolution. Lengths have 3 decimals in mm and 4 in inch. The blend tolerance option permits 0.001 mm, which is 0.00004 in, so an inch program writes `G64 P0`. A smoothing tolerance under about 0.0005 mm (mm) or 0.00127 mm (inch) does the same. LinuxCNC reads `G64 P0` as `G64` with no deviation limit.

Expected: write the smallest positive value (`P0.001` mm, `P0.0001` in), or refuse by name. Never write `P0`.

Evidence (upstream/main `f0bdc5109`):
- `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps:65` (min 0.001 mm), `:137-140` (`fu` rounding), `:396`, `:540`.
- `assets/posts/tormach.cps:562` has the same code.
- `crates/app/src/smoothing.rs:42-50` (finish = tolerance x 0.5, no floor).

Found by the post audit against the LinuxCNC manuals (#4130).

Done means: no tolerance in the allowed range writes `P0` in mm or inch, on both posts, and a test pins the smallest value.

title: Wire Contour: control-side wire offset mode (COMP records for the LN2W post)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
The Sodick LN2W post can write the control's wire offset (#4076): `G41` / `G42 Hnnn` before the lead-in and `G40` on the lead-out. The post reads a `COMP` record in the stream.

The app does not write a `COMP` record for a Wire Contour. `crates/app/src/posting_wire.rs` posts the wire-centre path and states compensation off. So no LN2W program with offset can come from the app.

Work:

1. Add a compensation mode to Wire Contour: "in computer" (the default, as now), "in control" and "wear".
2. For "in control", generate the part contour with a straight lead-in and lead-out that are at least the offset radius long. Write `COMP` records around each pass, with the radius of each pass.
3. Decide how the wire laws (kerf, threading, slug) judge a path that the control offsets (#1498). The register value is set at the control, so the laws must judge the path with the stated radius.
4. Add an MCP tool or parameter for the mode (`area:mcp`), or file `MCP: <command>`.
5. Add goldens for the square and the 2-axis parts with offset on, rough plus skims (item 4 of #4076).

Done means: the app posts an LN2W program with control-side offset from a Wire Contour, the wire laws judge it, and the existing goldens do not change.

Refs #4076. Safety floor: this changes posted G-code and a gouge check.

title: Docs: the release site tests failed at three cuts in a row, and nothing runs them before the tag

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: documentation
labels.description: Improvements or additions to documentation

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## The maintainer's words

2026-11-26: "Issue; P1; Docs bug; actions/runs/45742430230/job/139654523067 this is the third time now the docs/sites pipeline failed."

## What happens

The `site` job of `release.yml` fails at the step "Site tests" after the tag. The `pages` job then does not deploy the documentation. A person must repair the site on a `site/vX.Y.0` branch and deploy it again.

| Cut | Failed | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| v0.25.0 | #3271 | site-only branch |
| v0.26.0 | #3763 | #3768, `site/v0.26.0` |
| v0.27.0 | run 45742430230, job 139654523067 (#4106) | #4109, `site/v0.27.0` |

The v0.27.0 failures (104 tests, 4 failures and 2 errors):
- Two tutorial tests read a UI file that does not exist now.
- The icons `op-rotary-flow.png` and `tool-form-mill.png` were not in `site/static/icons/`.
- The operation reference had no section for `RotaryFlow`.

The site of v0.27.0 is repaired and deployed. This issue is about the cause.

## Cause

`python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests` runs in `.github/workflows/release.yml` only. No gate tier and no workflow on `main` runs it. A PR that adds an operation, an icon or a label can merge with a red site test. The release finds it after the tag. A tag cannot move.

## What to do

- Run the site tests in a gate that each PR and each push to `main` get: the quick, batch and release tiers of `cargo xtask gate` are candidates.
- Select them when the diff changes an input of a site test, for example `crates/`, `assets/ui/` or `site/`.
- Make sure that the post-merge skip rule does not skip them for a change under `site/` or `assets/`.
- Make the cut gate fail before the tag when a site test is red.
- A change of `.github/` needs the decision of the maintainer.

## Related

body:
Add a display-chord STEP and STL loader for user-supplied machine part bodies so CamCraft can show real vendor CAD meshes safely.

## Context
Machining-grade STEP import (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step_import.rs` and `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs`) meshes at 0.005 mm chord and refuses a file when one solid fails healing or contains open cosmetic shells (`SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`). Vendor machine STEP files commonly include sheet-metal enclosures and logos that fail machining-grade checks and produce millions of triangles at 0.005 mm chord.

## Scope
- Add a display-only mesh loader in `camcraft-sim` (using `camcraft-geometry::step` and the pure STL reader moved by `#3639`) that meshes STEP part files at a coarse display chord (default 1.0 mm, configurable within safe bounds) and enforces a per-machine facet budget (for example 100_000 to 150_000 triangles).
- Accept open cosmetic surface shells (`SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`) and skip unbuildable cosmetic sub-solids with named diagnostics when loading visual-only machine bodies.
- Add a `BodySource` tag for visual-only bodies so machine-part collision checks report `not judged` for any open or uncertified body and never claim a collision check passed on visual-only geometry.
- Refuse corrupt, non-finite, or oversized files (over `MAX_STEP_BYTES` or facet caps) cleanly by name with no panic.

## Done means
Unit tests load a closed STEP part and an open-shell visual STEP or STL part within the display triangle budget, refuse corrupt or oversized inputs by name, and verify that collision checks report `not judged` for visual-only bodies.

Depends on #2591 and #3639.

title: Iso-surface closed check: open_edges passes edges on four or more facets, so a zero-volume dual mesh is returned as closed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`iso::open_edges` counts only edges with an odd number of facets (after its 1e-9 weld). An edge on four or six facets passes, and so does a facet whose corners meet at the weld. Two decisions read it as "the mesh is closed":

- `iso::extract_with`: a dual mesh with no open edges is returned; otherwise marching tetrahedra stand in.
- `app::stock_export` (`extract`): a mesh with open edges is refused, not written. The STL export and the stock mesh cache read it.

So a mesh that is not a valid solid can pass both.

Measured on main a1c57b475. We logged three counts at both sites: odd edges, edges on more than two facets, and facets that collapse at the weld. We ran all `camcraft-sim` tests and the `camcraft-app` suites `stock_export`, `contour_stock_run` and `stepped_stock_rapid`: 937 passed, 0 failed. 20 meshes went through the two sites:

| Site | Meshes | Odd edges > 0 | Edges on 3+ facets > 0 | Collapsed facets > 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dual (in `extract_with`) | 11 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| marching | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `stock_export` | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The one is `stock_dual::a_body_under_one_cell_never_panics_and_never_opens`. A cube 0.5 mm a side at cell 1.0 gives a dual mesh of 6 facets and volume 0. It is three flat fins: pairs of back-to-back triangles, all six on one edge. `open_edges` is 0, so `extract_with` returns it, and the test's "closed or empty" check passes. Marching tetrahedra on the same samples give 24 facets, every edge on two facets, volume 5.19e-3.

The same blind spot hid #4107: there marching tetrahedra gave 11,394 collapsed facets and 5,799 edges on three or more facets with 0 odd edges.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let m = cube(Point3::new(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), Point3::new(0.6, 0.6, 0.6));`
2. `let f = SdfField::from_mesh(&m.facets, 1.0, FIELD_BAND).unwrap();`
3. `let tris = iso::extract_with(&f, 1.0, IsoMethod::Dual).unwrap();`
4. `iso::open_edges(&tris)` is 0. Weld on the 1e-9 lattice and count the facets on each edge: one edge is on six facets. The signed volume is 0.

Expected: a mesh that passes the closed check is a solid: every edge on exactly two facets, and no facet collapsed at the weld. Otherwise marching stands in (in `extract_with`), or the export refuses (in `stock_export`).

### Proposed fix

Add a sibling of `open_edges` that counts the edges, after the same weld, that are not on exactly two facets. A facet that collapses at the weld leaves an edge from a corner to itself, and that edge counts too. Use it at the two sites above. `open_edges` stays for its other callers.

From the measurement, the one behaviour change in the current suites is the one-cell body: its dual mesh is refused, and the closed marching mesh stands in. Pin: the steps above give a dual-method result in which every edge is on two facets (here the marching mesh), and a hand-built mesh of two cubes sharing one edge is refused by the new check while `open_edges` passes it.

### Version and OS

main a1c57b475 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

title: Windows: disk_recovery test compares a path with a mixed separator and fails

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens:
The test `disk_recovery::a_repaired_default_machine_file_is_read_again_through_the_disk_reader` fails on Windows. It is in `crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing/disk_recovery.rs` (from PR #4078, #2324). It passes on Linux and macOS.

Evidence:
- Windows quick check of main on host `bacon`, at `5c50f6721315`: one failure, this test.
- Repeat on host `winnie`, at upstream main `a1c57b475`: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test default_machine_missing`. 9 tests pass and this test fails:

```
panicked at crates\app\tests\default_machine_missing\disk_recovery.rs:60:5:
the reader must use the isolated folder: the default machine file 3axis-vmc.mch cannot be read (default machine:
3axis-vmc.mch in C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp\.tmpMvVxEv\assets\machines: The system cannot find the file
specified. (os error 2)) - mount a machine on the setup, or reinstall the file
```

Cause:
The test makes the folder path with `join("assets/machines")`. On Windows that gives `...\.tmpXXXX\assets/machines`, with a forward slash. The reader writes `...\assets\machines` in its message. The `missing.contains(machines.to_str())` check at line 60 then fails. The production reader is correct. Only the test is wrong.

Fix:
Make the path with `join("assets").join("machines")` in the parent part and in `check_disk_recovery`. Do not change the reader.

Done means:
- The test passes on Windows (`bacon`, `lenny` or `winnie`) and still passes on Linux and macOS.
- The test still refuses a reader that does not use the isolated folder.

title: Hurco WinMax post: opt-in tool pre-fetch (T word without M06 after each tool change)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found during the tester fix round of PR #2646 (issue #2573).

**What the tester asks:** The tester's Hurco programs pre-fetch the next tool after each tool change:

```
T110 M6
T104
```

**What Hurco documents:**

- Online help, Program Functions, "M6 Initiates Tool Change": when this NC parameter is Yes (the default), a `T` word without `M06` pre-fetches the tool. The carousel moves the tool to the ready position. The change occurs at the next `M06`.
- When this parameter is No, the control ignores `M06` and a `T` word alone changes the tool.
- The 2010 WinMax NC Programming manual (704-0116-310, page 4-1) gives the same two rules.

**Why PR #2646 does not add it:**

1. The post cannot find the next tool. The engine global `programTools` (`crates/post/src/post/options.rs`) is sorted by tool number and has each tool one time. It does not give the tool-change order.
2. On a control with "M6 Initiates Tool Change" set to No, a bare `T` word changes the tool at once. The program then cuts with the wrong tool. Thus the output must be opt-in and default off.

**Proposed work:**

- Give scripts the tool-change order (for example a `toolSequence` global, or a `nextTool` value at each `TOOL` record).
- Add a Hurco option `preFetchNextTool` (default off). Write `T<next>` on its own line after `T<n> M6`. Write nothing after the last tool.
- The option description names the "M6 Initiates Tool Change = Yes" condition.

Done means: with the option on, a three-tool program writes the next tool after each `T M6`; with the option off, the output is unchanged; tests pin both.

title: Cut runner: HotTamale (4 CPUs) stalls the debug build of the release gate; a cut loses an hour for each attempt

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Found at the cut of v0.27.0. The facts are on #3303 (comments of 2026-11-26T00:56Z and 01:26Z).

## What happens

The runner HotTamale took the `camcraft-cut` job of `cut.yml` two times (runs 45727701972 and 45732227750, commit `859dce67c`, branch `release/v0.27.0`). Each time the step `debug build (--no-run)` got a `STALL` row after about 1315 s. There was no `FAIL` row.

- HotTamale reports 4 CPUs, thus the gate uses 4 jobs.
- The debug build of about 1200 test binaries writes no output for more than 15 minutes on 4 CPUs. The watchdog (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN`, 15 minutes) then stops the step.
- The same tree passed on `main` (`9e21ed682`). The third cut run (45735766737) ran on wopr and passed. The v0.26.0 gate passed on wopr with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=24` (debug build 261 s).

Thus a cut can lose about one hour for each attempt on this runner, and the stall is not a defect of the tree.

## The decision is the maintainer's

One of these, or a different choice:

1. HotTamale does not have the `camcraft-cut` label. Only a runner with sufficient CPUs takes a cut job.
2. The watchdog limit for the build step of the release tier is longer, or the build step prints progress, so a slow runner does not stall.
3. `cut.yml` refuses a runner below a CPU count, with a clear message at the start of the job.

No agent changes the runner labels or the limits (`runners` skill). This issue records the facts for the decision.

title: Field iso-surface: marching tetrahedra leaves slivers that collapse at the 1e-9 weld when a cut floor lies on the sample lattice

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`iso::extract_with(f, step, IsoMethod::Marching)` (`iso.rs`, `tet`) puts a mesh corner a few picometres from a sample when a field value at that sample is almost zero. This happens when a cut floor lies on the sample lattice (the field's cell centres). The facets that share that sample then have two corners less than 1e-9 mm apart. They are not exactly zero-area, so `push` keeps them. After the 1e-9 weld that `open_edges` uses (and after an f32 export), they collapse, and the edges next to them are on three or more facets. The mesh is then not a valid solid.

`open_edges` counts only edges with an odd number of facets. An edge on four facets passes, so the existing closed-mesh tests do not see this.

Dual contouring (the default) is not affected in the same steps. Marching tetrahedra is reached by name and as the fallback when a dual mesh is not closed (`extract_with`).

Measured on main f8748d97d with a synthetic block (steps below):

| Floor height | Method | Facets | Collapsed after the 1e-9 weld | Edges on 3+ facets | Odd edges |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15.25 (on the lattice) | Dual | 305,928 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 15.25 (on the lattice) | Marching | 1,216,284 | 11,394 | 5799 | 0 |
| 15.1 (off the lattice) | Dual | 306,320 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 15.1 (off the lattice) | Marching | 1,217,748 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The field distance at the lattice sample over the floor at 15.25 is -1e-12. At 15.1 it is 0.15.

We found it in our own lane, which meshes field stock with marching tetrahedra at cell 0.254 mm. Every collapsed facet that we located had its shared corner on a lattice sample, at cut-floor heights, and none were on the mesh's clip box.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 30.0, 30.0, 20.0, 0.5)`. The lattice samples are at (k + 0.5) * 0.5, so 15.25 is one.
2. `simulate` four feed moves of a flat tool of radius 3 at z 15.25: from (4, y) to (26, y) for y = 8, 12, 16, 20.
3. `iso::extract_with(field, field.cell(), IsoMethod::Marching)`.
4. Weld the corners on the 1e-9 lattice (as `open_edges` does). Count the facets with two equal corners and the edges with more than two facets.

Expected: 0 and 0, as for the dual mesh and for the floor at 15.1.

### Proposed fix

In `tet`'s `cross`, snap the crossing to the sample when it is within a small fraction of the edge from it (for example, `t` below 1e-6 or above 1 - 1e-6). The coincident corner is then exact, and `push` already drops the zero-area sliver. Also let the closed-mesh check (or a sibling of `open_edges`) count edges on more than two facets, so that tests see this class.

Pin: the steps above give 0 collapsed facets and 0 edges on 3+ facets for `IsoMethod::Marching`, and the mesh stays closed (0 odd edges) with the same volume as before. We have not yet tested the proposed snap.

### Version and OS

main f8748d97d (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3

body:
## What happens

`assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:744-747`:
- G200 writes `Q395=+0`.
- G205 writes `Q379`, `Q253`, `Q208=+99999.999` and `Q395`.

## Which versions accept which parameters

From HEIDENHAIN's own change lists and cycle manuals:

- **Q379, Q253** (cycle 205): from iTNC 530 NC 340 422, TNC 640 -01, TNC 620 340 56x-01, TNC 320 34055x-06. **Valid on 340 490.**
- **Q208** (cycle 205) and **Q395** (cycles 200 and 205): only from iTNC 530 **60642x-04**, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05 (Q395 in cycle 200: 77185x-01). Source: "Cycle 205: Input parameter Q208 for retraction feed rate added" (iTNC 530 manual 670388-25, p. 13; 737759-24, p. 20).

So the post's G200 and G205 blocks are not valid on any iTNC 530 340 49x software. This includes the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (NC 340490-03). The programming station used in #3095 runs 606425-04, which is why it accepted the blocks.

Note: the iTNC 60642x-04 change list names the depth reference "Q359", but the example blocks of the same manuals show `Q395`. This is probably a typo in the list.

## Expected

- For iTNC 530 340 49x (and other controls before the versions above), write G200 without Q395, and G205 without Q208 and Q395.
- The control's dwell or retract defaults then apply, or the post refuses a requested behaviour that the old cycle cannot do, by name.
- The choice follows the control and NC software in the machine file (see the dialect issue filed with this one).

## Done means

- G200 and G205 for an iTNC 530 340 49x machine contain only the parameters of that software.
- A test pins both parameter sets.
- The changed goldens are listed in the PR.

Related: #3095.

title: DIN/ISO Heidenhain post writes no stop or M6 at a tool change on a manual-change machine (Picomax)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

On a tool change, `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:381-392` writes only `T<n> G17 S..` and then `M3`. It writes no retract, no `M6` and no `M0`. The next block is `G00 G40 G90 Z+<clearance>` with the length of the **new** tool.

The engine does not refuse this. `crates/post/src/post/machine_installation.rs:67-68` only passes `toolChangeMode` to the script, and the DIN/ISO post never reads it.

## Why it is wrong on the Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03)

- The machine has a manual tool change (`assets/machines/fehlmann-picomax55.mch`).
- The machine's programming manual changes a tool with `L Z+0 R0 FMAX M92`, then an XY park move with `M6`. TOOL CALL comes before the M6 move (manual p. 2-11 and p. 2-19).
- The machine parameters from the delivery CD (the machine parameter file) confirm it:
  - MP 7440 bit 0 = 0: the program halts at M06.
  - MP 7480.0 = 1: TOOL CALL only passes the T number to the PLC. TOOL CALL does not stop the program.
  - MP 950 / MP 4210.0: the tool-change height is M92 Z-0.05.

A multi-tool DIN/ISO program therefore runs on with the old tool in the spindle, and the new tool's length and speed are active. This gives a wrong Z and a possible crash.

The machine file selects the Klartext post, which stops with `M0`. The defect occurs when a user selects the DIN/ISO post for a manual-change machine.

## Expected

One of:
- The DIN/ISO post refuses by name when `toolChangeMode` is a manual mode; or
- it writes the manual change sequence: retract `G00 G90 Z+0 M92` (or the machine file's change position), then `M6` (a stop by MP 7440 on this machine).

Also add an engine law: a post that does not handle `toolChangeMode` is refused on a manual-change machine, so other posts cannot have the same defect.

## Done means

- A two-tool job on the Picomax machine with the DIN/ISO post either refuses by name or writes a retract and a stop before the second tool cuts.
- A test pins this. Automatic-change machines are unchanged (goldens byte-identical).

Source: review of the posts against the Picomax 55 programming manual and its machine parameters. Related: #3095.

title: Field engine refuses a wide tool's short move on the per-move cell ceiling; the column engine cuts it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord when its swept window, clipped to the cut region, spans more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells. The message asks the caller to segment the move. For a wide tool, the tool's own footprint already passes the ceiling. Then a 1 mm move is refused, and segmenting cannot help.

The column engine cuts the same move. `backend.rs` says that refusals are backend-independent. This refusal is reached by a valid short move that the column arm accepts.

Measured on 6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0; `field_cut.rs`, `field_batch.rs` and `field_sweep.rs` are the same on main 034e91b8b), a synthetic block, cell 0.254 mm, one 1 mm feed move of a flat tool 50.8 mm across:

| Engine | Result |
|---|---|
| Column | cuts |
| Field | refused on op 0: "a chord's swept window spans more than" 1 << 22 "cells at cell size 0.254 - the move is too long for one field update; segment it" |

The tool's footprint alone is about 201 x 201 cells. With the block's height in the window, a zero-length move would pass the ceiling too.

We found it in our own lane at the same cell size: a disc head 127.4 mm across on a 44.45 mm neck (through `simulate_undercut`) and a flat tool 50.8 mm across over 33.7 mm of stock. Both were refused on their first move.

### Why it looks like a policy limit, not a memory limit

`cut_batch` keeps only a brick-to-sweep list. `cut_brick` dismisses a brick that the sweep cannot reach by one test at the brick centre. The work of a wide tool's short move is the bricks that it meets. Memory does not grow with the window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 120.0, 120.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (60, 60, 25) to (61, 60, 25) with a flat tool of radius 25.4.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut.

### Proposed fix

Let the ceiling bound what segmenting can bound: the cells of the chord's clipped window beyond the cells of the tool at rest at the chord's start (the same clipping). A short move of any tool then passes. A long chord still refuses with the same message, and segmenting always brings it under the ceiling. Pin: the steps above cut on both engines. Keep a pin that a long chord of a normal tool still refuses.

The f32 cut twin (`cut_twin_work.rs`, `TWIN_MAX_CELLS_PER_CHORD`) states the same value. We would keep it as it is in this fix and list it as a follow-up, unless you prefer both in one change.

### Version and OS

6c9e5f1e7 (v0.26.0, source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

body:
The Sodick LN2W post (PR #4065, issue #4045) refuses control-side wire offset. The post writes only the wire-centre path. A machine owner (Sodick AQ600L, LN2W control) gave the rules for control-side offset on 2026-11-25.

Rules from the owner:
- H numbers are consecutive integers from `H001`. A 3-pass cut uses `H001`, `H002`, `H003`. The operator sets their values at the control.
- The lead-in must be at least the wire radius long (the same rule as a mill cutter radius).
- `G41`/`G42` goes on the lead-in line, or on its own line immediately before the lead-in. The own-line form is easier.
- `G40` must go on a lead-out move.

The owner's example:

```
G54 G90
G29
T91
T84
T94
C001
G42 H001
G01 Y10.
X0.
G40 Y0
```

Open questions for the owner (ask before code):
- What does `G29` do on this control, and is it required?
- Which condition number goes with which pass (`C001` here, `C000` in the earlier kit)?

Work:
1. The post accepts compensation "in control" and "wear" for the LN2W dialect. It writes `G41`/`G42 Hnnn` on its own line before the lead-in, with H = pass number (from `H001`), and `G40` on the lead-out move.
2. The post refuses a lead-in shorter than the wire radius, with a message that names the operation.
3. The wire-centre path stays the default. Mark 21 output stays byte-identical.
4. Goldens for the square and the 2-axis parts with offset on, rough plus skims.

Done means: an LN2W program with control-side offset posts in the owner's form, a too-short lead-in is refused, and the existing LN2W and Mark 21 goldens do not change.

Refs #4045. Part of the Sodick work in #617 and #1500. Do not start before PR #4065 merges (this changes the same post).

title: Sodick LN2W post: post a constant taper (setup table height, corner motion, lean side)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
PR #4065 adds the Sodick LN2W wire post (`sodick-ln2w.cps`). The review of head `b12db2f06` found that a tapered cut on that post is not safe yet. Thus the post refuses each tapered cut by name. This issue holds the work that is necessary to post a taper again.

What is necessary before the post writes `TP` / `TN`, `G51` / `G52` `A` and `G50`:

1. **The height of the work above the worktable, for each setup.** `TP` and `TN` are heights above the worktable. A value in the machine file is the same for each setup. A 20 mm part on a 5 mm fixture then posts `TP20.` and `TN0.`, but its planes are 25 mm and 5 mm above the table. Add a setup value (a command with its MCP tool), send it in the stream, and refuse a taper when the active setup does not state it.
2. **The corner motion of the LN2W control under `G51` / `G52`.** No source confirms that the control cuts a mitre corner. A control that rounds the lower corner cuts a different surface from the surface that CamCraft checked. The owner of the AQ600L can confirm it with an air cut. Then state the confirmed rule in `sodick-aq600l.mch`.
3. **The lean side.** The app signs the stream angle by `edm.taper_angle.positive`. The post must read that rule (mirror it into `machine.edm`) and map the side to `G51` (left) or `G52` (right). Add a case for `top_right`.
4. **The angle precision.** A nonzero angle below 0.0005 degree rounds to `A0.`. Refuse it, or use a precision that the control is confirmed to read.

The removed taper code and its goldens are in the history of PR #4065 (head `b12db2f06`): `taperWord`, `taperHeights`, `edm.table_to_part_bottom` and `PARAM WireBottom`.

Refs #4045, #2130, #4065.

title: Post-merge gate: skip the full build for docs-only and process-only merges

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` runs the full batch gate on every push to `main` (`on: push: branches: [main]`, no paths filter). A merge that changes only docs (`site/`, `docs/`, `*.md`) or process files (`.claude/`) starts a full build and test run (30-60 min on a self-hosted runner) that tests exactly the code of the commit before it.

Today this is worked around outside the repo: a script on one collaborator's machine (`pm-cancel`, every 20 min) cancels such runs after they have started. That spends up to 20 runner-minutes per docs merge, depends on one machine, and other forks don't have it.

Expected: a commit that changes no code does not start (or immediately skips) the batch gate, and says so in the run summary.

Options:
1. `paths-ignore` on the push trigger (`site/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `.claude/**`), plus `workflow_dispatch` for a forced run. Simple; GitHub then shows no run for that commit.
2. A first step in the existing `yield` job (beside `post-merge-skip.sh`) that diffs the commit against its parent and sets `skip=true` when no file outside those paths changed, with a notice "docs/process only - the previous run covers this code". The run exists and is green-skipped, which keeps "one run per commit" visible.

Option 2 fits the existing skip mechanism and Sarge's "one run per commit" (#3714) best. Either way a commit that touches code, `Cargo.*`, `xtask/`, `assets/`, `.github/` or build scripts must always run the gate.

Done means: a docs-only or process-only merge to main finishes its post-merge workflow in under a minute with a "skipped: no code changed" notice; any commit touching code or build inputs runs the full gate as today; the off-repo cancel script is no longer needed.

labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Why: new users on Discord keep asking the same orientation questions: what a post is, how it differs from the machine file, which post fits their control (e.g. a Flexicam router, a Sodick LN2W wire EDM), what file to bring from Fusion or SolidWorks, and where 3D printing fits. One overview page in the guide (`site/content/guide/`) would answer them and link to the detailed pages.

A draft was written and reviewed with the user on 2026-11-25 (a private page; its content is summarised here so the page can be written in the docs site).

Sections:
1. **The five steps:** CAD (SolidCraft, Fusion, SolidWorks, Onshape, FreeCAD) -> CAM (CamCraft, ...) -> post (`.cps`) -> control (PathPilot, Mach3/4, LinuxCNC, grblHAL, Fanuc, Haas, Heidenhain, Siemens, Sodick LN2W) -> machine; what each hands to the next (STEP/.sc, CL data / .camproj, .nc).
2. **Conversational:** programming at the control (PathPilot conversational, Hurco WinMax, Mazatrol, Haas VPS, Sodick); when to use it and when CAD + CAM is better.
3. **Kinds of CNC machines:** mill, 4/5-axis, router, lathe, plasma, waterjet, wire EDM, sinker EDM, with example machines and what CamCraft supports.
4. **3D printing:** STL/3MF -> slicer -> printer is out of CamCraft's scope; open-source slicers (PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer, UltiMaker Cura, Bambu Studio, SuperSlicer) and commercial ones (Simplify3D; resin: Lychee, Chitubox).
5. **Design files, native vs neutral:** .sc, STEP, .f3d, .sldprt/.sldasm, Inventor/CATIA/NX, STL, DXF, SVG and what CamCraft opens directly; **Dutchman** (https://dutchmancad.xyz/, https://github.com/dutchman-cad/dutchman) converts native CAD files to SolidCraft designs.
6. **Who covers which steps:** SolidCraft + CamCraft, Fusion, SolidWorks + CAM add-in, Tormach + PathPilot, Mach3/4.
7. **Machine file (.mch) vs post (.cps):** "what can this machine physically do?" vs "how does this control want it written?"; one post serves many machines.
8. **Tools:** catalog, library, holders, tool numbers; import/export `.camtools`, PathPilot `.csv`, Hurco `.TCM`.
9. **What goes in and out of CamCraft:** part model, tools, machine, fixtures, program, project.
10. **Machine + post pairs** shipped in CamCraft (Tormach, AltMill, Haas, Heidenhain, Sodick ...).
11. **Which post do I pick?** read the control model from the control; exact match, closest dialect, air cut first, then ask on Discord / open an issue.
12. **At the machine:** load the program, set work offset and tool lengths (setup sheet), prove it (air cut, single block, feed override).
13. **How you can help:** share machine/control models, the maker's manuals, what the control accepts in your own words, alarm messages, air-cut results, machine numbers. Do not share programs or posts made by other CAM software, their screenshots or docs, or NDA material.
14. **Glossary** additions: native file, Dutchman, CL data, dialect, work offset, tool offset, pocket/tool number, single block, dry run.

Done means: a guide page "Model to Machine" with the sections above, linked from the guide index and from `machines.md`, each product claim matching what CamCraft ships at that time, `zola build` clean.

body:
What happens: CamCraft has one Sodick wire post, "Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)". It writes the 1998 Mark 21 word set, including taper as `G74/G75` with `U V`. The current Sodick LN1W/LN2W controls (AQ400L, AQ600L) program taper as `G51`/`G52` with `A` and cancel with `G50`, with `TP`/`TN` for the table heights (Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual, Sodick Inc. 2012). A user with an LN2W machine who picks our only Sodick post gets taper words their control does not read the way the program means. The header only says "NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL"; it does not say which control the words are for.

Found when a Sodick AQ600L / LN2W owner dry-ran our kit (2026-11-25, see #1500).

Expected: the post's header (and its description in the post list) names the control it targets and states that LN1W/LN2W taper is not supported; a taper cut posted with this post states the same in its header next to the first taper word. Until the LN2W dialect (#4045) exists, that is a visible refusal-style warning instead of a silent mismatch.

Done means: every program from the Mark 21 post carries a header line naming the Mark 21 control and "LN1W/LN2W: not supported - taper words differ"; taper programs repeat it beside the first G74/G75; the post list description says the same; goldens updated; no motion or code line changes.

Refs #4045, #1500, #617.

title: Sodick wire: an LN2W post dialect and a Sodick AQ600L machine file

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Why: our Sodick post writes the 1998 Mark 21 word set. A machine owner dry-ran our kit on a **Sodick AQ600L with an LN2W control** and reported that the Mark 21 naming does not fit his control. The public **Sodick LN1W/LN2W operation manual** (Sodick Inc., 2012; covers AQ400L/AQ600L) states the LN2W program format.

What the LN2W manual states (summary; source for the clean-room record):
- **Taper:** `G51` (left) / `G52` (right) with `A<angle per side>`, cancel `G50`; the taper starts during the move to the first surface and returns to vertical on the next XY move after `G50`. `TP` / `TN` load the Table-to-Program / Table-to-Next registers from the program. (Our post writes the Mark 21 `G74/G75` + `U V` form: wrong for LN2W.)
- **Taper heights** are control settings: Table to Limit, Upper (follows Z), Lower, Program (worktable to part bottom), Next.
- **Program start (manual example):** `G54 G90`, `G92 X0 Y0`, `G29` (reference point memory for the AWT) before `T91` (thread), `T84` (high flush), `C001`, `G41`/`G42 H001`; skim passes change `C` / `H` and use `T85` (low flush); end `M02`.
- **T codes:** T82/T83 drain closed/open, T84/T85 high/low flush, T90 cut wire, T91 thread, T96/T97 fill pump on/off.
- **Wire offset:** G40/G41/G42 with H registers per pass.

Owner notes (2026-11-25, relayed): machine is an AQ600L, control LN2W; he wants `G0 Z0` at the top "to bring the top head down" - **held until he says what Z0 is on his setup** (the manual example has no Z move; the operator sets the nozzle-gap height), because a wrong Z move can hit the upper head.

What is needed:
1. A post dialect **"Sodick LN2W"** beside the Mark 21 one (the Mark 21 post stays for older controls): the start sequence above, G51/G52 A / G50 taper, TP/TN, H registers per pass, the T codes above.
2. A machine file **Sodick AQ600L** (travels X/Y/Z/U/V and table/work limits from Sodick's published AQ600L specification; taper height keys per #2130).
3. Goldens for the EDM test parts (square, 2-axis, taper) on the new dialect, and the dry-run kit refreshed for the owner.

Not in scope: the `G0 Z0` start move (until the owner defines Z0); COND.DAT condition selection (#3183).

Done means: the AQ600L machine posts the square, 2-axis and taper test parts with the LN2W dialect - taper as G51/G52 A + G50 with TP/TN - pinned by goldens; the Mark 21 dialect output is byte-identical; the dialect header still says NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL until the owner reports a clean dry run.

Refs #1500, #2130, #617.

What happens: every program from the Sodick wire post starts with the comment `(WIRE NOT THREADED AT START)`, and a few lines later writes `T91` (thread the wire by the AWT). A machine owner (Sodick AQ600L, LN2W control) read the comment as wrong: the program does thread the wire.

Done means: the Sodick post's threading comment matches its first threading word, the goldens that carry the header are updated in the same PR, and no motion or code line changes (byte-identical apart from the comment).

title: Tools: a cutter hand on the tool, so a left-hand drill or mill is refused or turned M4, not run M3

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
### What are you trying to do

Keep left-hand cutters in a tool library and not run them backwards.

A left-hand drill or mill cuts only under M4. A CamCraft tool does not state its cutter hand:

- `Tool` has `thread_hand`, but that is the hand of a tap's thread (#1453).
- The Thread operation has `cutter_left` and `spindle_reverse` (#988), but these are set on the operation and both default to right-hand. A left-hand thread mill from a library therefore runs M3 until the user sets both. The #988 refusal compares the two values with each other, so it can't see what the cutter really is.
- `posting.rs` calls `ask_reverse_spindle` for the Thread operation only. I found no way to run a drill under M4.

So a left-hand drill imported from another tool library looks like a right-hand one. It posts M3, and it rubs or breaks.

This is not rare. In the public Fusion tool libraries of 45 vendor catalogues (134,498 entries), 1,333 milling and drilling tools are marked left-hand:

| Tools | Number |
|---|---|
| drills | 1,262 |
| center drills | 51 |
| multi-row thread mills | 20 |

The drills' names do not say that they are left-hand; only the library's hand field does.

I read the source at v0.26.0, and `posting.rs` and `tools.rs` on main at 49bfcaea. I did not run a left-hand tool on a machine.

### How you imagine it working

1. A `cutter_hand` field on the tool (`right` by default, `left`), for the rotating kinds. It is separate from `thread_hand`: a left-hand tap keeps its field.
2. The tool gate refuses a left-hand cutter by name for each operation that can't run M4. This step alone closes the gap.
3. The Thread operation reads the hand from the tool. `cutter_left` is then not stated twice, and the M3 refusal judges the real cutter.
4. The Drill operation runs a left-hand drill under M4 with `ask_reverse_spindle`. Posts without `millSpindleReverse` refuse it by name, as they do for #988 today (in 0.26.0, `fanuc`, `mach4`, `mazak` and `sinumerik-810m` declare it).
5. `.camtools` steps its version only for a library with a left-hand cutter, as it did for left-hand taps (`LEFT_HAND_VERSION`). An older build then refuses the file and does not read the tool as right-hand.

Steps 1, 2 and 5 are the useful first part. Steps 3 and 4 can come later.

Related: #988 (M4 thread mills), #1453 (left-hand taps), #897 (drill kinds).

Found while writing a Fusion 360 to CamCraft library converter, which skips these tools for now.

title: Stock: a box side a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets an extra column of material

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
### What happened

The column count of a stock box is a plain ceiling: `(extent / cell).ceil()`. A box side that is a few ulps longer than a whole number of cells gets one more column, although the box edge falls only femtometres into it.

Example: a 12.7 mm side read two ulps long (`f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2)`) over a 0.254 mm cell gives a ratio of 50 plus about 1e-14. The ceiling gives 51 columns, not 50. The box edge falls about 3.6e-15 mm into column 51.

A side reads a few ulps long after a rigid move in floating point, for example a blank moved into a setup frame and back.

Three places count the columns this way:
- `Dexel::block` (column stock).
- The cell-ceiling gate of the field block (`backend_build.rs`).
- The exact carry read `History::read` (`carry_exact.rs`).

Effects:
- Column 51 is a full cell. Material stands up to one cell (0.254 mm) past the box edge.
- The carry read of the same box also counts 51 columns.
- A mesh export that clips the last column to the box edge gets a column about 3.6e-15 mm wide. A weld at 1e-8 mm collapses its facets: edges on three or more facets and zero-area facets. A mesh check then rejects the stock. We saw this on our fork's own mesh export.

Expected: a box side within a relative 1e-9 of a whole number of cells gets that whole number of columns. A real part of a cell still gets its column.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let x0 = -f64::from_bits(12.7f64.to_bits() + 2);`
2. `let stock = Stock::block(Backend::Column, x0, 0.0, -0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 0.254).unwrap();`
3. Read the column arm: `nx` is 51. Expected: 50.
4. `stock.top(0.1, 0.5)` is 5.0. Expected: NaN, because x = 0.1 mm is outside the box.

### Proposed fix

One shared count, `cells_across(extent, cell)`, in `stock_sim::kernel`:

```rust
let r = extent / cell;
let k = r.round();
if k >= 1.0 && (r - k).abs() <= 1e-9 * k { k } else { r.ceil() }
```

Use it in `Dexel::block`, in the field block's cell-ceiling gate, and in `History::read` (with `.max(1)`, so a thin box keeps one column). We have this change on our fork with four pinning tests in `stock_sim/cell_count_tests.rs`. Each test fails on the plain ceiling (51 against 50). We claim this issue and will open a draft PR from a branch `issue/N-whole-cell-count`.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (wrong stock at a box edge, with a workaround: snap the box to whole cells before the block), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor), `area:sim`.

Done means: a pinning test makes a column block from a box side two ulps longer than 50 cells and gets 50 columns, no material past the box edge, and the same count from the carry read.

title: UI link: a local user who reads a stale discovery file can still spoof the window

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
﻿A follow-up from the review of PR #3971.

PR #3883 (merged) proved the link token without disclosure: the hello carries a siphash proof, the window answers its own proof, and the raw token never crosses the wire. This closes the wire-disclosure path.

## What remains

Issue #3874 names a local user who reads a stale discovery file. That user knows the token from the file, so they can compute every proof. The CLI learns a stale entry is stale only after a connect fails. A false server on the freed port of a crashed window answers and proves, and the CLI sends its tool calls to it.

The PR review of #3971 states the same limit: "Use an authentication exchange that proves prior knowledge of the secret without disclosing it first, or use a transport that verifies the peer identity." A shared secret that both sides read from the file cannot separate the peers by cryptography on this transport.

## Fixes to consider

- Before the connect, check that the pid in the file is alive, and remove the file of a dead pid. This removes most stale entries. The design exists on branch issue/3874-link-proves-token (PR #3971).
- On Windows, a named pipe with a user-only ACL replaces the TCP port. The CLI asks the kernel which process serves the pipe and refuses any other peer before the token proof. The full design, its tests, and two incidental bug fixes (a pipe-instance handle leak; overlapped waits on a NULL hEvent) are preserved on that branch and PR.

Suggested labels: P3, area:mcp, effort:high, source:agent.

title: Wire EDM: a tangent arc lead-in and lead-out

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What happens now.** A Wire Contour lead goes in a straight line from the start hole to the nearest point of the wire path. On a circle, this lead is radial. The wire stops and turns at the entry point. This can leave a small dwell mark on the part.

**What we want.** An option next to the straight lead: a short tangent arc lead-in and lead-out. The lead goes from the start hole to the start of a short arc. The arc meets the contour tangentially at the entry point. The lead-out is the mirror of the lead-in. The wire then enters and leaves without a stop at the contour.

**Rules.**
- The straight lead stays the default. The arc lead is opt-in. The existing goldens do not change.
- The arc radius has a stated rule (a user value with a default, limited by the hole distance and by the kerf).
- When no tangent arc lead fits, the operation refuses by name. It does not clamp the radius silently, and it does not go back to the straight lead silently.
- The existing wire laws (the lead stays in the waste and clears the product by the kerf) and the simulation verifier check the arc lead.
- Posts: generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM write the lead arc as G02/G03. Sodick keeps its rule that the first move is straight: the move from the hole to the arc start is that straight move.
- The option has an MCP field, a project-file field (serde default; old projects do not change) and a UI row.

**Done means.**
- A die circle and a line+arc punch cut with the arc lead. The lead is tangent at the entry. The laws are clean.
- A hole that is too near and an arc that crosses the profile are refused by name.
- New post goldens for ISO, Sodick and G-EDM with the arc lead. The straight-lead goldens do not change.
- The MCP field and the project file round-trip the option.

Suggested labels (I cannot set labels): `P6`, `effort:high`, `area:2d`, `source:agent`.

Refs #3937

title: Tool meridian of a sharp taper or a drill misses the radial shoulder when the flute is shorter than the cone

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`Tool::meridian()` (`crates/tools/src/meridian.rs`) and `Tool::profile()` disagree for a sharp tapered mill or a drill when the flute length is shorter than the cone. The profile steps out to the full radius at the flute top. The meridian does not add that radial shoulder, so it ends at a smaller radius.

The review of PR #3929 found this class for flat and ball taper tips (review comment 7144791597). PR #3929 fixes it for the new flat and ball tips only (`crates/tools/src/taper.rs`, `meridian_points`). It does not change sharp tapers or drills, because that PR keeps their output byte-identical. The same missing shoulder stays on `main` for sharp tapers and drills.

## Why it matters

The two shapes describe the same tool. If code reads the meridian for a collision, gouge, simulation or solid, it sees a smaller tool than the profile and the real cutter. That can hide a contact. The filer has not traced each reader of the meridian; this needs a check before the priority is set.

## What to check

- Each reader of the tool meridian for milling tools (sim tool bodies, solids, fidelity checks, stamps).
- A sharp taper and a drill with a flute shorter than the cone: compare `profile()` and `meridian()` at the flute top. A test in the style of `taper::tests::short_flat_profile_and_meridian_agree` (PR #3929) shows the gap.

## Done means

For every tool kind, the meridian and the profile agree at the flute top, including the radial shoulder of a short flute. A test pins a sharp taper and a drill with a short flute. Any changed digest or golden is listed in the PR.

The account that files this issue cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set the priority (P1 if a collision or gouge check reads the meridian, else P3), `bug`, an effort label, the area label and `source:agent`.

Found while fixing #3929.

title: Wire EDM refuses any DXF chain with an arc or a circle

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## What happens

A Wire EDM contour on a DXF chain that contains an arc or a circle fails to generate. The maintainer reported it.

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Wire Contour1: invalid machining parameters: the selected DXF chain contains an arc or circle; the generic wire path requires straight segments
```

The refusal is made at `crates/app/src/operation/wire_sketch.rs:247`.

## Why it matters

A circle and an arc are the most common wire EDM shapes: a punch, a die opening, a hole. The generic wire path cannot cut either one. This blocks the basic use of the wire feature. The maintainer set the priority at `P1`.

## What is expected

- The wire path accepts an arc and a circle from the DXF chain.
- The path is cut as an arc: a wire machine interpolates an arc from its own block (G02/G03 with I/J or R), so the toolpath and the post carry the arc, not a long chord list.
- A full circle without a lead-in point has a start rule (a lead-in on the circle, or a slit), and the path says which.

## Related issues

- #3215: "Wire output writes no arcs: circles and fillets become G01 chords". The output side of the same class. This issue is the generation side.
- #3216: Wire Contour closing overlap, centre-line slit cutting, skims on open contours.
- #2702: G-EDM XYUV taper and 4-axis ruled wire post support.
- #2692: XYUV wire EDM swallowtail test fixtures.
- #2871: Example case: Wire Contour, and a taper that the machine refuses.

## What to check

- The refusal at `wire_sketch.rs:247`: which chain kinds reach it, and whether the generic path has an arc arm at all.
- The wire post vocabulary: a dialect that writes an arc block (G02/G03 with I/J) and the one that accepts only G01.
- The pin `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection.rs:219` asserts the refusal. It changes when the feature lands.

## Missing at filing

- The DXF and the operation parameters. Add them as a comment when the case is reproduced.

title: 2D Contour outside, several parts at one level: the rings after the first plunge through the pass link, with no note

labels.name: bug

body:
## What happens

An outside 2D Contour with entry Ramp or Helix enters its first ring by the entry. PR #3833 ramps the first ring of each level on the wall side.

Each ring after the first ring at the same level is reached through the pass link. `contour_link::ring_link` lifts, crosses and plunges straight down at the plunge feed. The posted program has an axial dive at each of these rings. No note says so.

This is the same fault as #3830 on the bore side. PR #3834 fixes the bore side only.

## Reading

Setup: no compensation, tool diameter 6 mm, stepdown 1 mm, 3 levels, bottom Z -3, ramp angle 5 degrees. Each part is a 16 mm square. The parts are 40 mm apart. Counts are plunge moves / axial dives, measured on a branch that has #3833.

| Entry | 1 part | 2 separate parts | 3 separate parts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ramp 5 degrees | 0 / 0 | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 |
| Plunge | 3 / 3 | 6 / 6 | 9 / 9 |

Ramp and Helix post no note about these dives. Helix posts only its stand-down note.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: `ring_to_ring`, then `ring_link`. The bore side asks for the entry. The wall side does not.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_link.rs`: `ring_link`, the lines after the keep-down proof (`guard`, then `MoveKind::Plunge`).

## Expected

One of these:
- Each ring after the first ring takes the entry (ramp or helix), by the wall-side ramp of #3833.
- Or the generator names the plunge in a note, as the bore side does for the tabbed case.

The compensation refusal of #3890 stays: control and wear compensation refuse Ramp and Helix on both sides.

title: Tool library file: .camtools drops the drawn cutter (ToolCutter) on export and import

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
**What happens**

A tool can have a drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`, #93 slice 2). The project file (`.camproj`) keeps it in `ToolDto::cutter`. The tool library file (`.camtools`) does not keep it:

- `export_tool_library` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`, lines 94-129) writes the tool, its `body` or `holder`, and no `cutter`.
- `parse_tool_library` (lines 137-191) does not read a `cutter` key. `LibraryTool` has no cutter field.
- `ImportTools` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs`) sets the tool and its body only.

Thus an export and an import give a tool without its drawn cutter.

**Expected**

- Export writes the drawn cutter of each tool that has one, as `[z, r, arc]` points (the `.camproj` form).
- Import reads it and judges it against the tool numbers (`tool_body_wire::cutter_from_dto`, the same check as the project loader). A cutter that disagrees refuses the whole file by tool name.
- `ImportTools` Add, Update and Replace set the cutter, and undo restores the previous cutter, in one undo step.
- A file with a cutter says a new version (5). An older build then refuses the file by version. It does not drop the cutter silently.
- A file without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower, so older builds still read it.

**Why it matters**

- Since #852 the stack laws read the drawn neck of a cutter. A tool that loses its cutter in a library round trip is a different tool for those laws.
- The form mill kind (#3369, plan step D2) keeps its outline in this field. Without this fix, a form mill exported to a library loses its shape.
- This is a leftover of #93 (see the research comment on #93, item 4).

**Done means:** a tool with a drawn cutter makes the same tool after export and import; a cutter that disagrees refuses the file by name; Update replaces the cutter in one undo step; a library without a cutter keeps version 4 or lower. Pinned by tests in `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs`.

Part of #3663 (plan step D3a). Refs #93.

The filer (qsmits) cannot set labels. A collaborator: please set a priority and an effort label, and `source:agent`. The parent #3663 is `P4`. This changes a file format, thus `effort:high` by the AGENTS.md effort table.

title: 2D Contour: with control or wear compensation, check that Plunge and Arc entries cannot reach the wall before G41/G42 engages

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent

labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## Problem

PR #3890 (#3888) refuses a Ramp or Helix entry or level transition under control or wear compensation, because those moves reach the wall before G41/G42 engages. The same PR notes an open gap: the Plunge and Arc entries also move under G40 before compensation engages. Nobody tested them against a register larger than the nominal radius, or a positive wear value.

If one of those moves can reach the finished wall before compensation is active, the program cuts the wall silently. That is the same class of defect as #3888.

## Check and fix

- For control and wear compensation, find each move between the end of the rapid and the first move with G41/G42 active, for each entry type (Plunge, Arc, Ramp, Helix) and each side (wall side, bore side).
- Prove from the posted G-code that each such move stays at least the maximum allowed register difference away from the finished wall. Or move the compensation engage before it, or refuse the combination by name.
- Pins on the posted G-code, with an oversized register and a positive wear value: the finished wall is not touched before G41/G42 is active.

## Notes

- Follow-up from PR #3890 (#3888) and the post-merge safety read of #3833.

title: 2D Contour wall-side ramp runs on the ring before G41/G42 engages, so control and wear compensation do not apply to it

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d

body:
Found in the post-merge safety review of PR #3833 (merged 2026-11-24, Fixes #3829).

## What happens

An outside 2D Contour with entry Ramp or Helix now ramps onto each level by a zig-zag along the lead-in and the ring.

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_wall_ramp.rs` lines 45-47: the zig-zag path is `flatten(s.e2, &[lead, walk].concat())`. When the ramp run is longer than the lead-in, the legs go onto the ring, next to the finished wall.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_step.rs` lines 127-134: `engage_level` posts these moves before the lead-in.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs` lines 336-348: the compensation span starts at `walk_at - 1`, the lead-in move. `contour_comp::push_span` (`contour_comp.rs` lines 172-178) engages G41/G42 on that move.

The ramp moves are thus posted with G40 active, at the cutter centre that the generator calculated from the nominal tool diameter. `contour_comp::door` (`contour_comp.rs` lines 59-93) does not refuse a ramp or helix entry under control or wear compensation.

Example: a Linear lead-in of 5 mm, a 1 mm level step and a 3 deg ramp angle give a run of about 19 mm. One out-and-back leg is about 9.5 mm, so about 4.5 mm of each leg is on the ring.

## Why it is unsafe

Under control compensation the register holds the real tool radius. Under wear compensation it holds the wear delta. The operator sets these values to put the wall where the program says. The ramp moves on the ring do not get the register value:

- Control: if the real radius is larger than the nominal radius, the ramp cuts the wall by the difference.
- Wear: a positive wear value has the same result.

The finishing pass under G41/G42 cannot restore the cut material. The verifier and the simulation read the nominal centre moves, so the overcut passes silently. Before PR #3833, the wall side had only a graze dive at the lead-in start, which is away from the wall.

## Expected

Do one of these:

- Keep the wall-side ramp on the lead-in only when compensation is in the control. If the lead-in is too short, graze and say why.
- Or refuse a ramp or helix entry on the wall side under control or wear compensation, by name, in `contour_comp::door`.

The bore side (`contour_bore.rs` lines 124-133, `zig_onto` along the same path) has the same pattern. Check it in the same fix.

## Done means

- No feed move of a compensated outside contour runs on the ring outside the G41/G42 span, or the generator refuses the combination by name.
- A test in `crates/motion/tests/machining2d.rs` sets `Compensation::Control` and `Compensation::Wear` with entry Ramp and Helix on an outside contour. It fails on the current main.

Refs #3833, #3829.

- **With Arc:** the automatic dead-end ramp is still there. There are 8 "ramp along the pass instead" entries from `descent_dive::entry_restart`, over 1411 mm². This is the same as before the PR. The maintainer's rule on #3748: remove each automatic entry that the user did not select.
- **With Plunge:** the tool plunges 9 times into uncut stock, with no note and no warning. The advice depends on `AirRoom`, and that case has no air room.
- The stand-in notes (`descent_dive.rs:272` and `:284`, `air_entry.rs:241-247`) are notes only. `entry_status_lines` drops them, and no Warning is posted. So the user sees nothing.
- Pins 2 and 3 of #3748 are green on `main` with this behaviour, so they do not pin it.

## Why P1

A plunge into uncut stock with no warning is an unsafe result that passes silently (Prime Directive). The maintainer ordered that each outcome issue of the #3741 family is P1.

## Fix

- Remove the automatic dead-end ramp for a selected Arc on a plain Outside pocket. If no air entry is possible, refuse the entry with a named diagnostic, or use a safe entry and name it in a **Warning**, not a note.
- A selected Plunge into uncut stock gives exactly one Warning that names the plunge, on the operation and in the status line.
- `entry_status_lines` shows each stand-in entry.
- Pins, red on `main` `1fe369fab` first: a plain Outside pocket with no stock (1) with Arc has no automatic ramp, or names it as a Warning; (2) with Plunge has a Warning for each plunge into stock.

## Notes

- Related: #3748 (closed by #3872), #3567, #3746, #3843.
- Review comment: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3872#issuecomment-7130985919

title: UI link on Windows: the CLI does not check that the window on a stale port is the real window

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 with a port that the OS selects (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). The discovery file `<pid>.json` holds the port and the token (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:44-57`). A window that crashes does not remove its file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:159-168` runs only on a normal drop). Only a new window with the same pid replaces it.

The CLI connects to each candidate file (`crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:165-174`):

- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:101-137`: `open` sends the token, then accepts any peer that answers `HELLO_OK`. The window does not prove that it knows the token.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:133-135`: after the hello, there is no read deadline.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/link_client.rs:207-210` and `:249`: `read_line` and `io::copy` read the answer with no size limit.

A different local user can bind the stale port on 127.0.0.1. That user then gets the stale token and the arguments of each tool call (for example file paths). That user can also send false tool results to the CLI, or a line with no end that makes the CLI use all memory. That user cannot run commands in a real window.

On Unix this risk does not occur: the folder is mode 0700 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:196-204`).

**Expected**

The CLI talks only to the real window. Possible fixes:

- The window proves that it knows the token (for example an answer that includes a hash of the token and a client nonce).
- Before it connects, the CLI checks that the pid in the file is alive, and it removes a stale file.
- The CLI reads each answer line with a size limit.
- Alternative: a named pipe with a user-only ACL replaces the TCP port (the decision in `docs/decisions/3751-cli-ui-link.md` names this option).

**Done means**

- The CLI refuses a peer that does not prove the token.
- The CLI reads answers with a size limit.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` starts a false server on a stale entry and shows that the CLI sends no tool call to it.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

title: UI link: a client without the token can hold the only link session for 5 minutes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found in a security review of PR #3861 (part 1 of #3751).

**What happens**

The UI link serves one client at a time. The token check is on the first line, but the same deadlines apply before and after the token check:

- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:181`: the link uses `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (5 minutes) for its listener.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:233-255`: `accept_loop` serves clients one after the other.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:283-351`: before the hello line, the read loop accepts up to `MAX_LINE` (16 MiB, line 56) and waits up to the idle window.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/listen.rs:330-334`: the token check occurs only when a complete line arrives.

On Windows the link is TCP on 127.0.0.1 (`crates/app/src/mcp/link.rs:221-226`). Each local user can connect to that port. A client without the token can connect and send no newline. It then holds the only session for 5 minutes. It can connect again after the drop. During that time, `camcraft-cli --ui` cannot reach the window. The app also buffers up to 16 MiB for an unauthenticated client.

No command runs, and the UI thread does not stop. This is a denial of service of the link only.

**Expected**

A client that does not send a valid hello line in a short time (for example 5 s) is closed. The hello line has a small size limit (for example 4 KiB). The 5-minute idle window and the 16 MiB limit apply only after the token check.

**Done means**

- A pre-hello deadline and a pre-hello size limit exist in `listen.rs`.
- A test in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs` connects, sends no hello, and shows that a second client with the token gets a session after the short deadline.

Refs #3751, PR #3861.

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Follow-up of #3843 / PR #3858, from the Opus safety review on PR #3858 (head `215d44a52`).

The law of #3843 (a 2D Offset whose "Pass starts at" is Inside or Outside takes the Arc entry unless the user selects another type) reads only the values before and after an edit; it does not see what the request named. Two doors miss it:

1. **The create door does not get the law.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:308-311`: `add_operation` patches the seed and calls `CreateOperation` directly. Probe: `add_operation {"kind":"2D Offset","params":{"pass_start":"outside"}}` gives `pass_start: outside`, `entry: helix` - the bug of #3843 at another door.
2. **An explicit Helix in the same request is replaced with Arc.** `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:323-324`: `edit_operation` merges the patch onto the current params, so the law cannot see a named entry. Probe on a new 2D Offset: `edit_operation {"params":{"pass_start":"inside","entry":"helix"}}` gives `entry: arc` - the user's named choice is overridden. A GUI page that sends the start side and the entry in one edit would have the same problem (only the MCP door was probed).

One rule closes the class: the door tells the law whether the request named an entry, and the create door applies the same law against the seed.

Done means: both probes above give the expected entry (Arc for 1, Helix for 2), each pinned by an MCP test in `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start/start_side_entry.rs`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/3843-start-side-arc.md` lists the named-entry case.

1. The `PR-reviewer` agent file lists the light lane as a required step with its own line in the report table, and the review comment has a fixed row for it.
2. The merging session checks for the light-lane row before it flags a PR ready.

The finding comes from the review lane of 2026-11-24. The three PRs above are merged or in review. Their light lanes were green (#3790, #3802) or not run (#3837).

title: 2D Contour with level link keep_down: generation takes minutes, almost all of it in verify_bodies
