body:
Reported timing on a plate with about 8.5k facets and inside rings (entry helix, helix
angle 4, level keep_down):

| rings | time |
|---|---|
| 1 | 4 s |
| 2 | 7.6 s |
| 4 | 20 s |
| 8 | 70 s |

That is about n^1.5. `max_stay_down` does not help.

Finding. All timings are from a debug build (local repro, 43,268 facets, 1/8 in tool, entry helix, helix angle 4,
`level: keep_down`, `transition: ramp`, inside rings picked on the plate):

| rings | moves | kernel `contour()` | `verify_bodies` | `generate` total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 541 | 1.7 s | 29.3 s | 31.1 s |
| 2 | 2,173 | 2.3 s | 115.2 s | 117.7 s |
| 4 | 4,909 | 3.9 s | not isolated | 378 s |
| 8 | 9,865 | 6.1 s | not isolated | 1,018 s |

Without keep_down: 65, 150, 305 and 630 moves; 5.6, 8.9, 21.5 and 54.2 s.

- The kernel is not the cause: 6 s for 8 rings.
- About 94 percent of the time is `verify_bodies` in `generate.rs`. It costs about 54 ms for each
  move with 43k facets, with or without keep_down. The cost is linear in the move count.
- Keep_down posts 8 to 15 times more moves for the same rings (the ramp legs), so it is
  8 to 15 times slower. A slower growth than linear in the rings comes from the larger rings.
- `solid_hits` already has a `SolidIndex`. The slow sub-step inside `verify_bodies` is not isolated.
  It needs a profiler inside `verify_bodies`.

Needed: find the slow step in `verify_bodies` for a long ramped path, or cut the move count of a
keep-down ramp. A STEP model with 4 to 14 mm through holes reproduces it (not attached here).

title: Bore: choose the entry (plunge, ramp, helix) and cap the descent with the approach angles

body:
The Bore operation always enters a hole with a straight plunge
(`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, the Bore arm: `entry: Entry3D::Plunge`).
The motion kernel already supports Ramp and Helix for bores
(`crates/motion/tests/bore_ramp_angle.rs`). The user cannot select them.

A second problem stops a ramp on a small hole. The kernel ring ramp allows at most
64 out-and-back legs (`MAX_ZIG_LEGS`). A 3.2 mm hole with a 3.175 mm tool has a
cutter-centre ring of 0.0125 mm radius. A 5 degree ramp needs about 73 legs for 1 mm of
stepdown. The ramp gives up and the tool dives axially. Measured on main: Ramp and Helix
on that hole post 6 axial dives and the note "the ring is too short to ramp at the angle".

Needed:
- `entry` on the Bore operation: plunge (default), ramp, helix.
- The links' approach `ramp_angle` and `helix_angle` cap every descent of the hole.
- The default stays plunge. A plunge Bore is written without an `entry` word, so
  earlier files do not change.
- A hole barely wider than the tool (ring radius 0.0125 mm) ramps at the cap.
- Arc is refused by name.

Done means:
- One Bore operation with entry ramp and angle 5 posts no feed descent steeper than
  5 degrees on holes from 3.2 mm to 6 mm with a 3.175 mm tool.
- The only axial move is the re-plunge down the column that the ring just cut, one for
  each level, and a note names it.
- A non-centre-cutting tool with the default (plunge) entry is still refused by name.

Found during #3746 (PR #3823), after the merge of #3818 (`7f4915a6d`, the in-plane ring links of #3747).

## What happens

Setup: `crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs`, `fig8_world()`, 2D Offset, Pass starts at Outside, EM-0800-4FL, the Arc entry (`offset_op_entered(..., PassStart::Outside, Entry3D::Arc)`).

The pass link at the end of a piece at (47.429, -39.000) does not keep down. The tool lifts to clearance and rapids 162 mm across the part to the next pass start at (46.482, 123.140). The same lift occurs at Z 12.000, Z 2.000 and Z 1.500. One more occurs at Z 1.500 to (-46.500, 123.542).

The link notes say:
- `link: the tool lifted to the retract plane 6 time(s) instead of the keep-down level/pass link - the in-plane link would cross a cut planned on that plane; ... (first lift at (47.429, -39.000), Z 12.000)`
- `link: the tool lifted to the retract plane 6 time(s) instead of the keep-down level/pass link - the in-plane link would leave the area that keeps the tool off the part; ... (first lift at (46.488, 123.257), Z 12.000)`

Each next start is in material. The entry code (`entry_restart`) tries, in this order:
1. the air entry of #3746;
2. the ramp along the pass;
3. a clear helix.

None fits, so the start is entered with the named plunge: `entry: the pass start (46.482, 123.140) at Z 12.000 is in material and the arc's lead room is blocked, and no ramp fits clear of prior cuts - plunged into material at the plunge feed`.

## Why the entry code cannot fix it

The start stands inside ring 0, the walk along the stock edge, which is cut first. Each in-plane lead from the air crosses ring 0 at the cut Z, and the verifier's Crossing law holds such a post. The start column has no room for a helix clear of the earlier cuts. The piece is too short for the ramp. Only a link that stays down through cut material (for example along ring 0) reaches the start. That is link or order code (`pass_link`, `ring_links`, `level_order`).

## Done means

- `fig8_outside_offset_has_no_plunge_into_material` (`crates/app/tests/offset_pass_start.rs`) is green. Remove its known-fail marker in the same PR.
- On fig8 Outside, no pass link lifts across the part to a start in material without a named reason that the status line shows.

title: Column stock: simulate copies the whole cut history on each call, so a program cut one move at a time is quadratic

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_sim::cut::simulate` (the column engine behind `Stock::simulate`) copies the stock's whole cut history at the start of each call:

```rust
let mut history = dex.history.as_deref().cloned();
```

The history holds every cut so far. It grows with each call. A caller that cuts a program in small steps (one move for each call) thus copies a longer history at each step. The total time is quadratic in the number of moves.

Expected: the time of a program cut one move for each call is near the time of the same program cut in one call.

### Evidence

We run `camcraft-sim` from a fork as the stock engine of a batch verifier. The verifier reads the stock before each cutting move, thus it cuts one move for each call.

- A 3-axis job on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, 137,940 moves: one call takes 2 s. One move for each call ran for more than 1800 s, and we stopped it.
- With the history grown in place (below), one move for each call takes 6 s. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a column stock: `Stock::block(Backend::Column, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 20.0, 10.0, 0.1)`.
2. Make 4000 short feed moves across the block.
3. Cut them in one `simulate` call. Then cut them on a second, new block with one `simulate` call for each move.
4. Compare the times. The second cut is much slower, and the gap grows with the number of moves.

### Proposed fix

Take the history out of the stock, grow it in place with `Arc::make_mut` (this copies it only when another stock shares it), and put it back. On a refusal, truncate the cuts to their old count and put the history back, so the stock stays as it was (`add_ops` only appends cuts). We have this change and a pinning test on our fork. We will open a PR from a branch `issue/3819-history-in-place` if you accept the claim.

Not in scope: `carried::clip_columns_under` uses the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (slow with a workaround: cut in one call), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor).

Done means: a pinning test in `camcraft-sim` cuts 4000 moves one call at a time on a column stock. Each column top is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, and the time stays inside a linear budget.

body:
Found during #3746.

## What happens

#3746 gives the Arc entry of a start-side pass (2D Offset, "Pass starts at" Inside or Outside round a part) a plunge in air outside the stock box and a G17 arc onto the first ring. The change is in `pocket_started_on` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`, `air_entry.rs`).

The avoid route (`pocket_avoid_started_on`, used when the op has fixtures or clamps to avoid) builds its own `Motion` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, near the `with_cleared_links` call). That `Motion` has no air room. Thus with fixtures, the Arc entry keeps the old behaviour: "the arc's lead room is blocked - axial dive on the floor instead". The dive is named, so it is not silent.

## Why it was not done in #3746

The air outside the stock box is proved free only of the part. On the avoid route, a fixture or a clamp can stand outside the stock box. The air room must subtract the keep-outs of the avoid spec (grown by the tool radius) before a lead can use it.

## Done means

- The avoid route passes an `AirRoom` whose legal area is the cutter-centre area joined with the air outside the stock box, less each keep-out grown by the tool radius.
- A pin on the dog-bone part with a clamp outside the stock box: the plunge stands outside the box by the tool radius plus the approach distance, and the lead does not touch the clamp.

title: Adding a catalog tool above the mounted machine's max rpm says nothing until verify holds the post (EM-0300-2FL 15000 rpm on a 10000 rpm 770MX)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

On a mounted Tormach 770MX (ML) (`spindle_max` 10000 rpm), `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` and `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0400-2FL" }` copy the catalog's 15000 and 12000 rpm into the document as they are. Nothing says they are above the machine: the `add_tool` reply carries only the holder note, `add_operation` and `generate` add no note, and the first word of it is the machine check at verify / post, which holds the program:

```
machine Tormach 770MX (ML): 2 limit problem(s): 2D Adaptive1: tool EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the machine's 10000; 2D Contour1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs 12000 rpm, above the machine's 10000
```

The block itself is right (the Prime Directive holds: no over-limit S word is posted). The defect is that it comes last, after the work is generated, and that the other paths that set a speed already hold it to the machine and say so:

- `apply_cutting_data` / `suggest_cutting_data` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs`, `compute`): "45094 rpm held to the machine's 10000".
- the Feeds tab spindle row (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs`, `hold_to_machine`): "spindle speed N rpm held to the machine's maximum M".

Only adding a catalog tool (MCP `add_tool`, `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` -> `AddTool::with_holder`) takes the catalog rpm with no reading of the mounted machine. The verify problem also does not say what to do about it (edit the tool's speed, or `apply_cutting_data`).

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate. Script `b.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script b.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("set_stock", {box: {dx: 37.4, dy: 37.4, dz: 5.27}});
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0400-2FL"})));   // no rpm word
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Contour", tool: "EM-0400-2FL", source: "simple"});
cam.generate();                       // generates, no rpm note
cam.log(JSON.stringify(cam.verify())); // gate ok:false, the problem above
```

## Expected

When a tool is added (MCP `add_tool`, and the UI's add from the catalog) while a machine with a `spindle_max` (or `spindle_min`) is mounted and the tool's rpm is outside it, the reply / status says so at once, e.g. `"warning": "EM-0300-2FL runs 15000 rpm, above the Tormach 770MX (ML)'s 10000 - the post will be held; set the tool's speed (edit_tool) or apply_cutting_data"`. The machine check at verify keeps blocking as now, and its problem line names the same fix. The tool's rpm is not changed silently by the add (a library speed stays what the user stated; the warning tells them).

## Where

- `crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs` `add_tool` (the reply has `note` for the holder only).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs` `AddTool` (where a note like the holder note can be built from the mounted machine).
- `crates/post/src/machine/check.rs` and `crates/app/src/posting_default_machine.rs`: the "runs N rpm, above the machine's M" problem text, which could name the fix.
- For comparison: `crates/app/src/cutting.rs` (`compute`, the clamp with a note) and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/spindle_row.rs` (`hold_to_machine`).

Related: #3457 (the lathe sibling: catalog TN-1600-0R8's 3000 rpm over the Tormach 15L's 2500, a first post held).

Priority P7 (a late refusal that could say more and an owed warning; the block is correct and the workaround is plain: edit the speed or apply cutting data). Effort medium: a note in one command's reply and the UI add path, plus the problem wording, with a test; posted G-code, the machine check and the gate do not change (if the fix instead clamps the rpm at add, it changes posted S words and is effort:high by the safety floor).

Done means: with the Tormach 770MX (ML) mounted, `add_tool { "catalog": "EM-0300-2FL" }` returns a warning naming 15000 rpm and the machine's 10000, the UI's catalog add shows the same text, a tool within the range gets no warning, and verify still blocks the post with a problem line that names the fix; pinned by a test in `crates/app/tests/`.

title: 2D Adaptive on the stock: a stock margin narrower than the tool is refused as "pocket is narrower than the tool", with no band, width or fix named

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found by the reporter in v0.26.0 via the AI Chat panel (2026-11-23). Reproduced headlessly with the 0.26.0 `camcraft-cli`; the same code is on `main`.

## What happens

A 2D Adaptive on the stock (source `stock`, no boundary picks) around a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate, stock from **fit stock** (2 mm per side, top Z 3.27), with a 3 mm end mill (catalog `EM-0300-2FL`), on the Tormach 770MX (ML), refuses at generate with:

```
2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool
```

The refusal is right (the area to clear is the 2 mm band of stock around the part, and a 3 mm cutter has no legal position in it), but the message does not say that. There is no pocket in this job, so "pocket" points the user at the wrong thing. It does not say which area is narrow, how wide it is, by how much the tool misses, or what to change. The in-app assistant read it as a missing boundary selection or a too-small helix radius (0.6 mm), and neither is the cause.

Readings (box stock, `dz` 5.27, side margin m per side, same tool and op):

| margin per side | result |
|---|---|
| fit stock (2 mm, Z -2..3.27) | refused: "pocket is narrower than the tool" |
| 1 mm | refused, same text |
| 2 mm | refused, same text |
| 3 mm (= tool D) | generates (Offset rings fallback, notes) |
| 4 mm, 6 mm | generates; the #1655 band note and corner note appear |

So the band check that #1655 added (`machining2d::unreached_note` through `operation::keep_law::narrow_noted`) names a narrow band only when some other part of the area produced a path. When the whole area is one band narrower than the tool, the generator refuses first, with the bare sentence, and the band note never runs.

## Steps to reproduce

`simple.step` is a 25.4 x 25.4 x 1.27 mm plate STEP (any plate of that size works). Script `a.js`, run with `camcraft-cli script a.js`:

```js
cam.import("simple.step", "simple");
cam.call("load_machine", {builtin: "Tormach 770MX (ML)"});
cam.call("fit_stock", {});            // 29.4 x 29.4, Z -2..3.27: 2 mm per side
cam.call("add_tool", {catalog: "EM-0300-2FL"});
cam.call("add_operation", {kind: "2D Adaptive", tool: "EM-0300-2FL", source: "stock"});
cam.generate();
```

Output: `generate: 2D Adaptive1 - could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: pocket is narrower than the tool`. Replace `fit_stock` by `set_stock {box: {dx: 31.4, dy: 31.4, dz: 5.27}}` (3 mm per side) and it generates.

## Expected

A refusal that says what is narrow and what to do, e.g. "2D Adaptive1: the stock around the part is a band 2.000 mm wide, narrower than the 3.000 mm tool (plus 0.000 mm stock to leave): no cutter position fits. Widen the stock to at least 3.000 mm per side, use a tool under 2.000 mm, or cut the outside with a 2D Contour." The same refusal stays a refusal (no path is emitted); only its words change. Where the area is a real pocket (a part source, a closed boundary), the text names the pocket and its narrowest width the same way.

## Where

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs` `pocket_started_on` (the site this job hits: `non_sliver_center(region, off)` empty -> `GenError::Invalid("pocket is narrower than the tool")`), and the same bare sentence in `adaptive_avoid.rs`, `pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, `rest_prior.rs`, `corner_relief_spur.rs`, `adaptive/rest/mod.rs`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs` `narrow_noted` / `machining2d::unreached_note` (#1655): already measures the band; it could word the refusal when the whole stock-around-part area is one band.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate/run_job.rs` `name_outside_entry_refusal` already adds advice to this sentence, but only for Outside containment (#2232), not for the stock source.

title: 2D Offset one ring set: full-width cuts where the rings of two lobes merge (fig8 waist), and the narrow note does not name them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Found while fixing #3744 (one ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside). Related: #3743.

## What happens

The one ring set of #3744 is the offsets of the part. At a concave place of the part, the offsets of two lobes merge. At the merge, the corner of each ring moves by more than one stepover from the corner of the next ring. Thus some cuts there take the full tool width.

Readings on `testdata/models/fig8.step` (the `offset_pass_start` heavy fixture: EM-0800-4FL, stock margin 5 mm, Outside containment):

| Pass starts at | full-width cut points (`flanks::full_width_points`) |
|---|---|
| Outside (one ring set, #3744) | 495, all at the waist band, Y 40 to 70 |
| Inside (the same ring set) | 10686 (most are the first ring along the part wall, which is named) |
| Outside before #3744 (rings parallel to the stock box) | 0 |

- The full-width cuts at the waist are not named. `level_order::full_width_at` measures the distance to the nearest cut (1.9 tool radii). The ring arms near the merge are inside that distance, so the "narrow" note does not come.
- This is a load issue, not a gouge. The gouge and crossing checks are clean on this pass.

## Expected

- The rings at a merge do not take the full tool width. One option: clean-up rings or a smaller local step between two ring corners that are more than one stepover apart (Held, "On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining", 1991, covers the merge of offset curves).
- A cut that still takes the full width is named on the path, by the same law that the flanks meter uses.

## Pins

- `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` (heavy): #3744 moved its reading from 0 to the bound "at most 520 points, all in the waist band". The fix sets it back to 0.
- A motion pin on a synthetic two-lobe part that reads the full-width points at the merge, for Inside and Outside.

Done means: the two pins are green, and no unnamed full-width cut is left at a ring merge.

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Aur package; should rebuild the Linux build that comes before it and not rebuild it again from scratch.. Waste of time and action credits." He set the priority P2.

## Problem

In `release.yml`, the AUR package step compiles CamCraft again from the source. The `linux` job of the same run has already built the same release binaries from the same tag. The second build costs time and billed GitHub Actions minutes (AGENTS.md: the minutes are budgeted).

## Expected

- The AUR package uses the Linux release binaries that the `linux` job of the same run made. Use an artifact (`actions/upload-artifact` in the `linux` job, `actions/download-artifact` in the AUR step), or the release asset of the same tag.
- The AUR package does not run `cargo build` again.
- The PKGBUILD that we publish stays correct for AUR users. If the AUR rules need a from-source PKGBUILD, publish it unchanged, and only the CI check of the package uses the prebuilt binaries. Record which way was chosen, and why, in `docs/decisions/`.
- The packaged binary is byte-identical to the binary in the Linux release asset. A check compares the checksums.

## Notes

- This changes a file in `.github/workflows/`. Use the `runners` skill. Add no trigger. The maintainer ordered this change.
- Measure the minutes of a tag run before and after, and put the numbers in the PR body.
- Test the change with a `workflow_dispatch` dry run, not with a new tag.

Done means: a PR that adds an operation, a post hook or a manifest property without its site page makes a gate red before the cut.

title: camcraft-cli: a --ui flag sends commands to the running UI, and --skill installs an AI skill for the CLI

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
## Request

The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-23. His words: "Make the camcraft-cli able to interact witht he ui. By adding the flag --ui, so it instead sends it commands directly to the UI and changes gets reflected in the UI. This allows for alot better interaction and end2end testing, for dealing with UI improvements and for endusers also doing setups. The CLI improvements should come with a --skill <folder,claude,copiplot> install creating a AI skill for working with the CLI tool."

The maintainer set the priority P2.

## Part 1: `camcraft-cli --ui`

- With `--ui`, the CLI does not run the commands in its own headless world. It sends them to a running CamCraft UI.
- The UI runs each command through the same undoable command history as the GUI ("Everything Is a Command"). The change shows in the UI at once, and Ctrl+Z undoes it.
- The CLI prints the result of each command and returns a non-zero exit code on an error, as in headless mode.
- When no UI is running, the CLI gives a clear error. It does not fall back to headless mode silently.
- Uses: end-to-end tests of UI changes, agent-driven checks of the UI, and set-up of a project by a user from a script.

Questions to decide (record each in `docs/decisions/`):
1. The transport: a local socket or a named pipe. Find the UI with a discovery file in the user's data folder. Bind only to the local machine.
2. Security: accept only local connections from the same user. Use a token in the discovery file. Never listen on a network port.
3. The protocol: reuse the MCP tool surface (`crates/app/src/mcp/`) so that the CLI, MCP and the GUI call the same commands. Do not make a second command set.
4. Several UI windows: select one by project path or process id.
5. Windows, Linux and macOS from the same source ("Stays buildable everywhere").

## Part 2: `camcraft-cli --skill <target> install`

- `<target>` is one of `folder`, `claude` or `copilot`.
- `folder`: write the skill files into a given folder.
- `claude`: install the skill where Claude Code reads skills, for the user or for the project.
- `copilot`: install it where GitHub Copilot reads custom instructions.
- The skill text comes from one source in the repository, and it lists the CLI verbs, the `--ui` mode and examples. Relate it to #1947 (single-source AI agent skills) and to the existing `camcraft-mcp` skill.
- A test checks that the installed skill names each CLI verb that exists (a drift test).

## Pins

- A UI test starts the app through the test harness, sends one command with `--ui`, and checks that the UI state changed and that undo restores it.
- A CLI test with no running UI checks the clear error and the exit code.
- A test for each `--skill` target writes into a temporary folder and checks the files.

## Notes

- This is new design (an IPC transport and a protocol), thus effort:max.
- Slices are permitted: part 1 first, then part 2.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at: Arc in the plane is the default entry; a user-selected Helix, Ramp or Plunge gives a warning; remove the automatic #3577 ramp

labels.name: bug

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3746 (the air entry) and #3747 (the in-plane links).

## The maintainer's words

"you would never helix on a outside cut.. as you dont need to "lead in" like that.. so an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut, starting outside the stock boundary with a given value."

From the #3741 comment: "An Outside cut never uses a helix entry, and it does not use a ramp entry." Pin: "an Outside pass has no helix move and no ramp move into material, and that each entry starts outside the stock boundary."

## What happens

A start-side pass can still enter by a helix or a ramp at four places:

1. The first entry of a level: `descent.rs:216-286` (`plan_arm`) with the user's Helix or Ramp; `descent.rs:131-136` (a helix stands down to a ramp).
2. The #3577 dead-end ramp: `level_ramp_entry.rs:100-127` (`dead_end_ramp`), marks at `level_order.rs:143-145`, plan check at `level_rings.rs:108`, call at `ladder_links.rs:188-191`. Decision: `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md`.
3. The #2265 solid restart between passes: `ladder_links.rs:200-211`.
4. The centre-cutting law stand-ins: `descent.rs:137-148`.

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part; see the #3741 research comment): Outside on `main` has 366 ramp moves (13 dead-end ramps). On `47aa341ff^1` the same 13 re-entries were plunges or helices.

## Fix approach

1. After #3746 and #3747 a start-side pass has one entry for each level (the air entry) and no re-entry into uncut stock. The dead ends of #3567 do not exist with the contour-parallel rings of #3744.
2. Remove `dead_end_ramp`, its marks (`ramp_starts`) and its plan check. Update `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md` with a "superseded by #3741" line.
3. On a start-side pass, a restart that would need a helix or a ramp lifts and uses the air entry, or the op is refused with a named reason. It never helixes or ramps into stock.
4. Rewrite the pins of `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs` that assert a ramp ran. The late-entry pin counts every entry into stock again (no ramp exemption).

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_pass_has_no_helix_or_ramp`: Inside and Outside on the dog-bone part and on `testdata/models/fig8.step` have no helix move and no ramp move below the material top.
- `start_side_entries_start_outside_the_box`: each entry of a start-side pass starts outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance.
- `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` (existing, `pass_start_engagement.rs:181`) stays green with no ramp exemption.

Effort `high`: removal of one entry law and its pins, under the safety floor.

Done means: the pins are green, `dead_end_ramp` is gone, and the #3567 decision file names #3741.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at: rings stay at depth and link in the plane; lift only when an in-plane link hits the part or a fixture, with the reason named

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max

body:
Part of #3741. Builds on #3744 (one ring set). Covers Inside and Outside (and Auto through #3744).

## The maintainer's words

"Simulation show that the path approach breaks down, instead of "going around the" object in the plane, it "lifts over" it picking up the contour ont he other side and starts ramping down back and forth to the desired depth again.. Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

About Inside: "And it also does a shit ton of uncessary lifts.."

The rule from the #3741 comments: each ring goes around the part in the plane and stays at depth. Where a ring is split, the link stays in the plane when the path is clear. A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason.

## What happens

1. The 2D Offset uses `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`; `crates/app/src/operation/types/links.rs:65-67`). Its pass link is `Link::Retract`. `pass_link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs:154-225`) then lifts at every pass break, with no proof and no reason (`:161-163`, `:182`).
2. With `Link::KeepDown`, `link_proof` (`:243-261`) and, for a start side, `through_cut` (`:230-237`, `cleared_links` at `pocket.rs:346`) refuse a link between two Outside pieces that end on the part wall: the chord crosses the part.
3. The planner joins two pieces only when `linkable` (`level_order.rs:110-151`). Each other piece is a new pass, thus a lift.
4. After each lift the re-entry is the #3577 dead-end ramp (`ladder_links.rs:188-191`) or the #2265 solid restart (`:200-211`). This is the "ramping down back and forth".

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part, 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level; see the #3741 research comment):

| Pass starts at | lifts (Retract) | re-entries | lifts (KeepDown) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 13 | 14 |
| Inside | 8 | 7 | 7 |
| Auto | 7 | 6 | 7 |

The Outside counts are the same on `e313aa663` (#3353). #3577 changed only the kind of re-entry.

## Fix approach

1. With the one ring set of #3744, link ring k to the next ring at depth by a stepover link in the cut plane. The link runs through the band that the next ring cuts.
2. Make the in-plane link the rule for a start-side pass, whatever the pass link of `Links::PLANAR` is. A lift needs a reason.
3. Where the stock edge splits a ring, link the pieces in the plane through cut material or air when the chord clears the part and the fixtures.
4. Lift only when each in-plane link would hit the part or a fixture. Tally the reason with `st.tally.lift(why, ...)` and show it on the status line.
5. Check #3423 (P7, lifts between pieces) and close it as covered when this merges.

## Pins (red first)

- `start_side_rings_do_not_lift`: on a part with no split ring (a disc in a larger stock box), Inside and Outside have no lift and no re-entry on one level.
- `dogbone_start_side_lifts`: on the dog-bone part, count the lifts and re-entries of one level for Inside and for Outside. Each lift has a named reason in the notes. Expected: 0 lifts when each link clears the part.
- `lift_reason_is_named`: a fixture across the in-plane link gives one lift, and the status line names the fixture.

Effort `max`: a new linking law with a collision proof, under the safety floor.

Done means: the three pins are green, and the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` with Inside and Outside has only lifts with a named reason.

body:
Part of #3741. The entry sub-issue of #3741 uses this parameter.

## The maintainer's words

"an outside cut would default to a ARC or straight approach in the plane of its cut, starting outside the stock boundary with a given value."

From the #3741 comment: "The approach starts outside the stock boundary by a given distance. That distance is a parameter with a default value." Pin (1) of that comment: "the plunge XY is outside the stock box by at least the tool radius plus the approach distance".

## What happens

No such parameter exists. `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` (`Approach`, fields at `:80-110`, defaults at `:225-245`) has `arc_radius`, `arc_sweep`, `arc_xy` and `plunge_height`, but no distance from the stock edge. The MCP approach DTO (`crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs:292`, `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:389`) has no such field.

## Fix approach

1. Add `approach_distance` (mm) to `Approach`. Recommended default: 2.0 mm, the same as `DEFAULT_PLUNGE_HEIGHT`. A value below 0 or not finite is refused when the command is made ("Validate early"). Record the default in `docs/decisions/`.
2. Add it to the project file (`crates/app/src/project/approach.rs`, as `Option<f64>`, absent = default, so old files load unchanged), to the digest (`crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs`), and to `EditOperationParams` (undoable).
3. Show it on the Lead in / Lead out page (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/lead_page.rs`) when Pass starts at is Inside or Outside.
4. Add the MCP field under `links.approach` and to the `camcraft-mcp` skill table.

## Pins (red first)

- `approach_distance_round_trips`: save and load keep the value; a file without the field loads the default.
- `approach_distance_edit_undoes`: an edit through `EditOperationParams` and its undo restore the previous value.
- `mcp_sets_approach_distance`: the MCP tool sets and reads the field; a negative value is refused with a message.
- A UI structural test: the row is present for Inside and Outside and absent for Auto.

Effort `high`: a new parameter in several crates, with its command and MCP field. It changes posted G-code through the entry sub-issue.

Done means: the parameter exists with its default in motion, the project file, the UI and MCP, and the four pins are green.

title: 2D Offset Pass starts at: one contour-parallel ring set for Auto, Inside and Outside; the choice changes only the start point and the ring order

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Part of #3741. The other sub-issues of #3741 build on this one.

## The maintainer's rule

His words (chat, 2026-11-23): "The only thing that differs and inside and outsided strategy is actually where the tool starts.. inside the bounding box, or outsided the bounding box. Why there is different cut strategies between outside, inside and auto (which is insane) is strange.."

Also: "contour-parallel offset rings from the outside in toward the selected contour" (the #3741 body, Expected).

## What happens

"Pass starts at" selects one of three different ring planners. Each gives a different set of rings.

- Dispatch: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs:101-120` (`ring_plan_ramped`).
- Auto: `pocket_plan.rs:20-36` -> `waterscan.rs:62` (`waterline_passes`). It offsets the whole cutter-centre area from both edges. In a long narrow band the loops collapse to thin back-and-forth loops. The maintainer sees "zigzag or raster-like moves in the long side areas".
- Outside: `level_rings.rs:188-203`. The rings are offsets of the outer edge only (the stock box). The part cuts each ring into open pieces that end on the part wall.
- Inside: `level_rings.rs:169-187`. The rings are offsets of the part, grown out. They are parallel to the selected contour.
- Other start-side switches: `pocket.rs:308-347` (`cleared_links`, `ramp_starts`), `pocket_avoid.rs:147, 209-210`, `pocket_hsm_start.rs:42-63`, `pocket_hsm.rs:61-62, 92-100`, `level_order.rs:143-145`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:982, 1102` (the stock band goes to the plan only when the start is not Auto).

Readings (synthetic dog-bone part in an 80 x 50 stock box, D8, stepover 2, one level; see the #3741 research comment):

| Pass starts at | floor runs | runs that end on the part wall |
|---|---|---|
| Outside | 14 | 14 |
| Inside | 8 | 0 |
| Auto | 7 | 1 |

This started with #3353 (`e313aa663`). It is not a regression of #3577.

## Fix approach

1. Make one ring set for the three choices: the contour-parallel rings, at the distances `off + k * stepover` from the selected contour (the part), cut by the cutter-centre area of the stock box. This is the ring set of the Inside branch today.
2. The rings that the stock edge cuts are open pieces. Keep them in the same set.
3. Inside walks the rings from the part out (k up). Outside walks them from the stock edge in (k down).
4. Auto selects one of the two start points. It does not select a different planner. Recommended rule: Auto = Outside when the stock box is larger than the cutter-centre area on all sides (open air around the stock), else Inside. Record the rule in `docs/decisions/`.
5. Remove the Auto-set fallback of `level_rings.rs:113-118` for the start sides, or make it give the same ring set. A leftover area gets clean-up rings of the same set, not a different planner.
6. Delete the start-side switches that only exist because the ring sets differ (`cleared_links`, the dead-end marks). The linking and entry sub-issues of #3741 replace them.

Check the other users of `level_pieces` and `plan_passes` (2D Pocket, `pocket_avoid`, the 3-D pocket levels). #3743 reviews all 2D ring planners. This issue is the 2D Offset slice of that review.

## Pins (red first)

- `inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: on the dog-bone part, Inside and Outside give the same multiset of rings (each ring as a closed or open polyline, compared within 1 um after a start-point and direction normalisation). Only the ring order and the start point differ.
- `auto_is_inside_or_outside`: Auto gives exactly the path of Inside or of Outside on the same part.
- `outside_rings_follow_the_part`: on the dog-bone part, no Outside floor run ends on the part wall, except at a ring that the stock edge cuts.
- `fig8_start_sides_have_no_crossing`: on the committed `testdata/models/fig8.step` (through the existing test loaders), Inside and Outside give no `Warning::Crossing`. (The maintainer's Inside run gave 414 Crossing warnings on a private model. The synthetic part gives 0.)

Effort `max`: a new ring planner contract for three choices, under the safety floor (it changes posted G-code).

Done means: the four pins are green; Auto, Inside and Outside of 2D Offset call one ring planner; the decision file records the Auto rule.

body:
## Problem

The quick gate compares the worktree against the local `main` branch. In this repository, agents do not pull in the main checkout while a gate runs (#1201). Thus the local `main` can be many commits behind `origin/main`.

When the base is stale, the diff holds many files that the branch did not change. The quick gate then falls back to the batch plan.

## Seen

On the branch of PR #3738, the local `main` was `d66400b78`. The diff against it had 2056 files. The quick gate fell back to batch. The change itself touched only `xtask/`.

## Expected

The quick gate uses the merge base with `origin/main` (after `git fetch`), or it warns when the local `main` is behind `origin/main`.

## Notes

- `gate heavy --base main` can have the same problem.
- A test must pin the choice of the base.

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the context read for #3694 (the same defect in the Haas post).

## What happens

Each of these post scripts writes a mm feed as a whole number (`Math.round`): `fanuc`, `doosan-dnm`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `tormach`, `linuxcnc`. The tap feed is pitch x spindle speed (`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:33`), and the stream keeps 0.001 mm/min. The post rounds it. Example: M1.4 x 0.3 at S115 has the exact feed 34.5; the post writes `F35`. The pitch that the control cuts is F / S, so the pitch is wrong by 1.45 percent.

Not affected, by the same read: `mach4` (one decimal; check that one decimal is sufficient), `fanuc-lathe` (feed for each revolution, four decimals), `heidenhain` (refuses a pitch that it cannot write).

## Expected

The F word of a tapping block gives the exact feed for the pitch and the speed, or the post refuses the pair by name.

## Done means

- A test for each of the six posts pins the tapping F word for 34.5 and 133.2 mm/min.
- The format of the F word obeys the decimal point rule of each control (#3690).
- `mach4` is checked with a feed that needs three decimals.

Refs #3694, #3690, #3692.

title: Post scripts other than Haas write a whole-number F word without a decimal point

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post

labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
**What happens**

#3681 fixed the Haas post: each F word now has a decimal point (`F600.`). The scripts below still write a whole-number feed with no point (`F600`). This table comes from a read of origin/main 6866890b6.

| Post | F formatter (lines) | Whole-number F has a point? |
|---|---|---|
| carvera.cps | `ff` 84, `fw` 87 | no |
| doosan-dnm.cps | `ff` 193-196, `fw` 200, `feedWord` 1047 | no |
| fanuc.cps | `ff` 155-158, `fw` 162, `feedWord` 968 | no |
| fanuc-lathe.cps | G98: `capWord` 688 -> `fm` 683; G99: `feedWord` 313-318 -> `fr` 270 (`pt`) | G98 no; G99 yes |
| grbl.cps | `ff` 87-90, `fw` 93 | no |
| grblhal.cps | `ff` 93-96, `fw` 99 | no |
| heidenhain-klartext.cps | `rate` 61-68, used at 277, 306 | no for a whole value |
| heidenhain.cps | `ff` 70, `fw` 84 | no |
| linuxcnc.cps | `ff` 141-144, `fw` 147 | no |
| mach3.cps | `ff` 92-95, `fw` 98 | no |
| mach4.cps | `ff` 103 (`trimDec(..., keepDot=false)`) | no |
| mazak.cps | `ff` 128-131, `fw` 135 | no |
| sinumerik.cps | `ff` 83-86, `fw` 89 | no |
| tinyg.cps | `ff` 93-96, `fw` 99-107 | no |
| tormach-lathe.cps | `feedWord` 227-230 -> `fr` 186-189 | no |
| tormach-plasma.cps | `ff` 60, `feedWord` 300-306 | no |
| tormach.cps | `ff` 109-112, `fw` 115; A-axis `floorWord` 890-893 | no |

These scripts are correct already or have no F word: sinker-iso.cps (keeps a point), agie-native.cps (stub), sodick-wire.cps and wire-iso.cps (no F word found).

**Why it can be wrong**

On a Haas control, Setting 77 scales an integer F word (#3681). No public manual of the other controls was checked for the same rule. Some controls read an integer F as a whole feed, so the output can be correct there. A control with a setting like Haas Setting 77 reads the feed wrong.

**What should happen**

For each post, find the public programming manual of the control:
- If the manual says that the control scales an F word with no point, add the point. Make that control a `P1` defect, in its own issue or here.
- If the control cannot read a point in an F word (for example Klartext or a GRBL dialect), keep the present form and record the source.

**Done means**

- Each row has a cited manual section, and the post writes the F form that the manual specifies.
- Each changed post has a test that fails on an F word in the wrong form.

Found during #3681 (PR #3689).

body:
Found while working #3453 (issue-worker-high). The coordinator set P1: the verifier passes an unsafe entry silently.

## What happens

A 2D Contour with tabs posts a feed plunge of 18 mm into sheet that no level above cut (#3453, #3678). `verify` gives `ok: true` with no findings.

Evidence:

- The reporter of #3453 ran `verify` on CamCraft v0.25.0 (q07, MDF bracket, 18 mm sheet). The result was `ok: true`, no findings, for a plunge from Z2 to Z-18 with a 2.8 mm crescent of uncut sheet beside the cutter.
- After the #3453 PR, the motion fixture `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` shows two tab window dives with the full tool disc in uncut stock: Z12 -> Z-18 at (-5.165, -4.266) and (-4.796, 44.676), stepdown 4.5 (#3678 has the tables).
- Code read (context pack of #3453, origin/main 44c13a01d, not changed since v0.25.0):
  - `crates/motion/src/plunge_law.rs:91`: `guard` returns at once for a centre-cutting tool. A centre-cutting tool is the default (`approach.rs:256`, `tool_table.rs:138`).
  - For a tool that is not centre-cutting, the law reads the axis core only (`plunge_law.rs:56`, reach `tool_r * (1 - CORE)`), not the full disc.
  - `crates/sim/src/verify/`: no law compares a feed plunge depth with the stepdown, or with the floor that the cuts before it left under the disc. `rapids.rs` law (d) judges lateral rapids. `contact.rs:117-119` treats a plunge as the entry from air.
  - The wall-side entry notes are advisory (`contour_step.rs:120-127`).

Not verified here: a fresh `verify` run on the current main for the #3453 fixture. The worker ran motion tests only.

## Expected

`verify` names a feed plunge that goes deeper than one stepdown (or a stated limit) below the stock that the earlier cuts left under the full tool disc. The finding blocks the post, or it is a named warning that the user must see. A silent `ok: true` is not permitted.

Done means: a verify test with a recorded program that has such a plunge gives a named finding, and the #3453 catalog case gives the same finding until #3678 is fixed.

title: 2D Contour: a tab window dive plunges deeper than one stepdown into material that the levels above did not cut

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #3453 (issue-worker-high). This is part (2) of that issue. The coordinator split it out of the #3453 PR.

## What happens

A tabbed level of a 2D Contour enters each tab window at the start of the window's lead-in. The levels above cut that lead-in only at the ring start. At every other window, the lead-in start lies in material that no level above cut. The dive feeds from the retract plane to the tabbed level in one plunge move.

Fixture: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` (L-shape 40 x 40 with a 25 x 25 notch, Outside, `bottom_z` -18.3, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs 10 x 3, tool D6, Plunge entry, Arc lead r3, clearance 25, retract 12). "Floor" is the lowest level pass whose swept disc holds the point. "Disc floor" is the highest floor under the full tool disc.

Before #3453 (origin/main 44c13a01d), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 1 | (10.153, -6.000) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 2 | (-6.000, 29.525) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 | 3 | (21.000, 30.029) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | 0 | 18.0 | 2.501 |

After the #3453 PR (window 0 enters at the untabbed start; the tab layout ends the tabs on the spacing marks from the start), PLANAR links:

| level | window | entry XY | plunge Z | floor under centre | disc floor | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| -18 | 0 | (43.514, -5.802) | 2 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |
| -18 | 1 | (-5.165, -4.266) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 2 | (-4.796, 44.676) | 12 -> -18 | 0 | 0 | 18.0 | full disc |
| -18 | 3 | (18.186, 19.500) | 12 -> -18 | -15.3 | -15.3 | 2.7 | 0 |

With the stay-down ramp preset (`level: KeepDown`, `transition: Ramp`), the untabbed levels below the first do not cut the lead-in. After #3453, window 0 of the -18 level plunges 2 -> -18 at (43.514, -5.802) with the disc floor at -4.5: 13.5 mm below the floor.

With Lead None, each window dive is on the ring, in the kerf of the level above: 2.7 mm below the floor. That case is correct.

## Expected

No feed plunge of a contour goes deeper than one stepdown below the floor that the levels above left under the full tool disc at that XY.

## Proposed fix (from #3453)

- A guard on the wall-side graze dive (`contour_step.rs` `graze`) and the tab-window dive (`contour.rs`, window `k > 0`), for each level below the first level of its ring.
- Read the floor under the full disc from the moves that the builder has posted (flat feed passes and plunge columns).
- If the dive goes deeper than one stepdown below that floor, peck: plunge one stepdown, rapid up, plunge the next step. Say it in one note.
- The uncut floor is `min(entry top, first ring level + stepdown)`, so a first level and the shelf bands do not change.
- An alternative is to cut the window lead-ins on the levels above. Compare the two.

Done means: `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs` asserts that every descent of the three presets is at most one stepdown below the disc floor, and the pinned window 1 and 2 readings change to that.

body:
Found while gating the #2772 PR (PR #3674) on 2026-11-23. Reproduced on a clean worktree of `origin/main` with no diff, so it is not caused by that PR.

## What happens

The quick gate's per-crate prebuild machinery wedges deterministically on this machine: cargo 1.99.1's `rmeta` handoff across the gate's per-crate `--no-run` invocations deadlocks, so the prebuild steps never complete. The run hangs until the gate's stall watchdog fires.

The per-binary fallback works: the touched test binaries run one by one, and clippy runs clean. So the defect is in the prebuild handoff, not the suites.

## Done means

- The per-crate prebuild handoff completes on a clean checkout, or the gate detects the wedge and falls back to the per-binary path with a note.
- The stall rows name the wedged step.

Machine: Windows, rustc stable (cargo 1.99.1), sccache active. Observed twice: once on the PR worktree, once reproduced on clean `origin/main`.

title: A .camtools library cannot hold a form-profile mill, a blunt tapered mill, or a single-form thread mill without a pitch range

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
CamCraft at c5bb09ed13f8b63e691d3a5ed6fb0be6a64ee2aa.

## What other tool libraries store

Fusion tool libraries store three kinds of mill that a `camcraft-tools` definition has no field for:

1. Form mill: a drawn profile, a list of (radius, height) points from the axis at the tip, round the cutter and back to the axis. It covers thread mills, double-angle cutters, radius-profile cutters and any ground shape.
2. Tapered mill: a cone with a tip diameter (flat) or a corner radius (ball) at the tip, a taper angle per side and a shoulder diameter at the cutting length (tapered engravers, ball-tip tapered mills).
3. Single-form thread mill: one tooth in the profile; Fusion states no pitch range (the range is in the description text, if anywhere).

## What is missing

- `kind: taper` is a cone from a sharp apex. A tool with a tip diameter or a ball tip has no field; writing it as `taper` shifts the cone by half the tip diameter at every height.
- The drawn cutter outline (`set_tool_cutter_profile`, `ToolCutter`) exists in a project but a `.camtools` definition cannot carry it (`tool_edit` lists `cutter` as not here), so an arbitrary form profile cannot travel with the tool. `kind: form` is a lathe gauge.
- `thread_mill_single` needs `pitch` and `pitch_min`; a source that stores only the tooth has neither.
- Smaller: the dovetail check `top < sr` compares with no tolerance, so a neck that meets the flank exactly (head 6.096 mm, 1.4605 mm high, 45 degree flank, neck 3.175 mm) is refused by float dust: `3.048 - 1.4605 / tan(45 deg)` is one ulp under `1.5875`.

## Synthetic example

Form mill, mm: profile `(0,0) (2,0) (4,0.8) (2,1.6) (2,9) (4,11) (4,40) (0,40)` (one 43.6 degree V tooth on a 4 mm radius shank).
Tapered mill, mm: tip diameter 1, taper angle 30 degrees per side, cutting length 10, shoulder diameter 12.

## Ask

Any of: a `tip_d` (and ball radius) on `taper`; an optional `cutter` outline in the definition, judged by `cutter_profile::check`; an optional `pitch_min` default for `thread_mill_single`; a small tolerance in the dovetail neck check.

Until then Dutchman writes only the multi-form thread mill (rows of equal teeth at one pitch, read from the profile) and the sharp-tipped taper, and reports the others as not carried over.

## Measured

On a 97-tool Fusion library: 85 written, 12 not written (11 single-tooth form mills, 1 tapered mill with a ball tip). One multi-form thread mill and one dovetail now convert.

title: Two sessions dispatch onto one branch: add a branch-ownership guard

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Two sessions dispatched writers onto one branch three times tonight. The result was lost work, rejected pushes and a near force-push. The process needs an ownership guard.

## The cases

- #3567: an `issue-worker-max` held the claim from 22:14Z. A second worker (`issue-worker-high`) claimed again at 22:29Z and later pushed `e7ae538a3` to the same branch while the max worker had its own commit. The max worker's work was lost with its worktree.
- #3650: our rework worker (local `62809f42f`, on merge `68c10fc24`) and another session's implementation (`bfefff3bd` -> merge `5711344b0` -> `864897476`) diverged on `issue/2970-rotary-parallel-band`. The push would have been rejected or would have clobbered. The local design is held and recorded on the PR.
- #3577: a max-tier rework and a text-fix worker both wrote `issue/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end`; the text fix pushed `4d464e006` over the rework's head while the rework's independent duplicate stayed uncommitted.
- Same class, earlier: prepared branches were pushed by the coordinating session while the worker that made them was about to push (`#3391`, `#3494`).

## Harm

- A worker spends an hour, then cannot push.
- A push race invites a force-push, which the law forbids.
- Two reviews run on two implementations of one fix.
- The status reports disagree, and the coordinator relays a head that is not ours (as happened with #3650).

## Rule

Whoever claims the issue owns the branch. One writer for one branch at one time. A second session that finds a live claim or a live writer on the branch stands down and names the live writer.

## What to change

- A branch owner record that both sessions read before a dispatch: a claim comment on the PR (or the issue) that names the writer and the base, or a small `.claude/claims/issue-N` file with the writer, the branch and the head it started from.
- The coordinator checks the PR head and the owner record before every dispatch, and writes its own record.
- A push that the remote refuses because the branch moved is a STOP with a report, never a force-push.
- The skills that dispatch (`work-issue`, `review-prs`, `resolve-conflicts`, `merge-ready`) say where the record lives.

## Related

- #3567, #3577, #3650.
- The two-session setup itself: a second session and this coordinator both write the same repository.

title: Tool assemblies: derive cutting parameters, gauge length, and collision body from component frames

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What to build

Add the assembly geometry resolver that turns a component stack into a resolved `Tool`, gauge length, and `ToolBody`.

1. Classify `MCS_INSERT` as `CsysRole::Mounting` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs`.
2. Implement forward kinematics in `crates/tools` (pure rigid-frame math) and `crates/app/src/tool_assembly.rs`:
   - Start from the root component's machine-side `MCS` at identity.
   - Chain each child's `MCS` onto its parent's `CSW*` port.
   - Support an optional axial index angle (`z_rot_deg`) around the mating Z axis and an optional stickout `projection_mm` for cylindrical and collet mounts.
3. Normalize the assembly to CamCraft's tool frame so the active cutting tip (`CIP` for spindle tools, `CRP` / nose centre for turning inserts) sits at `(0, 0, 0)`.
   - Compute spindle gauge length as the `+Z` height of the root `MCS` origin in the normalized frame.
   - Derive turning `orientation` (LinuxCNC 1–8) from holder approach angle, holder hand, and insert shape when not overridden.
4. Derive the judged collision body (`ToolBody`) from all non-cutting components:
   - Combine STEP/STL/OBJ meshes and parametric `SpunProfile` holders into one `HolderProfile` (spindle) or `LatheClearance` (lathe).
   - Run size and tip-gap checks (`MAX_BODY_RADIUS`, `MAX_BODY_HEIGHT`, `MAX_TIP_GAP`) on the combined assembly, never on upper adapters alone.
   - Allow turning assemblies with a separate insert component to build `LatheClearance` from the holder mesh without requiring a manual `InsertZone`.

## Notes

- Depends on the component model sub-issue of #2452.
- Does not block on #1039: turning STEP components use explicit stored frames until turning STEP auto-alignment lands.

## Done means

- Tests in `crates/tools` and `crates/app` pin derived `Tool` cutting parameters, gauge length, spindle `HolderProfile` bands, and lathe `LatheClearance` bands for multi-component assemblies.
- Tests cover mixed parametric (`SpunProfile` / built-in holder) and STEP-mesh stacks, plus non-zero `z_rot_deg` indexing and `projection_mm` stickout.
- Tests pin named refusals for missing frames, ambiguous ports, cycle links, non-finite transforms, and bodies reaching into flutes.

Part of #2452

title: Tool components: ISO 13399 component model, ISO 1832 parser, and compatibility checks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What to build

Add the pure domain model and compatibility checks for reusable tool components in `crates/tools`.

1. Add `ToolComponent` with three ISO 13399 kinds:
   - `CuttingItem`: an indexable insert (`InsertSpec`) or a parametric solid `Tool`.
   - `ToolItem`: a turning holder, boring bar body, or indexable cutter body with one `MCS` and one or more `CSW*` insert seats (`InsertSeatSpec`).
   - `AdaptiveItem`: a spindle holder, collet chuck, collet, adapter, extension, or clamping unit with one `MCS` and one `CSW`.
2. Add normalized ISO/TS 13399-60 `ConnectionCode` types for `ADINTMS` and `ADINTWS` (steep tapers, HSK, PSC/ISO 26623, KM/ISO 26622, ER/ISO 15488, Weldon/DIN 1835-B, cylindrical shank, TTS, ISO 5608 rectangular shank, VDI, BMT, shell-mill arbor, and custom string).
3. Add ISO 1832 insert designation parsing (positions 1 to 7: shape, clearance, tolerance, fixing, size/IC, thickness, nose radius) and ISO 5608 seat parameters (clamping, shape, approach angle, clearance, hand, size).
4. Add pure compatibility checks (`check_insert_fit`, `check_coupling_fit`) and library query helpers (`compatible_parents`, `compatible_children`).
5. Refuse every mismatch by name. Each refusal states both component names, the mismatched property, the expected value, and the actual value.

## Clean-room provenance

Use only public standards (`ISO 13399`, `ISO 1832`, `ISO 5608`, `ISO 15488`, `ISO 26622`, `ISO 26623`, `ISO 12164`, `ISO 10889`, `JIS B 6339`, `ASME B5.50`, `DIN 1835`) and existing code in `crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs`.

## Done means

- Unit tests in `crates/tools` pin ISO 1832 code parsing for common turning and milling inserts.
- Unit tests pin valid insert-to-holder and coupling matches, plus `compatible_parents` ("holders that take this insert") and `compatible_children` queries.
- Unit tests pin named refusals for wrong shape, wrong clearance, wrong size/IC, wrong thickness, wrong clamping/fixing, wrong hand, and wrong coupling code.
- Pure Rust in `camcraft-tools` with no Flecs or file I/O dependencies.

Part of #2452

Found in the second safety read of PR #3058 (#1883). Refs #1882, #1885.

**Now (with PR #3058):**
- The operation has no standoff height. The cut plane is the top of the sheet (`crates/app/src/operation/waterjet_op.rs:96`, `cut_z = top`). Plasma has `cut_height`.
- The CL has no jet on/off record and no pierce dwell record. Travel moves are rapids at the clearance plane; lit moves are feeds. The pierce dwell and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only.
- No shipped post serves `Kind::Waterjet`. But a user script can declare `serves = ["waterjet"]` (`posting_serves/tests.rs:9`). That script gets this CL: no jet on/off, no dwell, and the nozzle tip on the sheet for a machine with a Z axis.

**Risk:** a nozzle that touches the sheet, or a jet that is not switched, on a machine that runs a user post. No shipped post can do it.

**Wanted (one of the two, the first is smaller):**
1. The post gate refuses a waterjet operation by name until the jet records (#1882) and the waterjet laws (#1885) are in. The refusal says what is missing.
2. Or: add the standoff height to the operation (validated above the sheet top) and the jet on/off and dwell records to the CL.

**Also:**
- The stock simulation skips Probe, Torch and Wire, but not Waterjet (`stock_sim.rs:288`). The nozzle goes into the dexel simulation as a cutter at the sheet top. `verify` gives no visible "not judged" note for a waterjet operation. A kind that no law judges must say so.
- Corner slow-down, taper and kerf lag are not modelled. Say so in the path notes or in the decision file.
- With a lead-in of 0 the pierce is on the kerf ring at the edge of the part, and no note says so.
- The label "In control (G41/G42)" uses G-code words (the plasma page has the same label). The row label "Tab position" is there two times (`waterjet_page.rs:110`).

title: 2D Pocket: warn at edit time when the tool cannot fit the pocket

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
What happens: `set_tool`, `add_operation` and the UI accept a tool that is too wide for a 2D Pocket. The generator refuses it later with "pocket is narrower than the tool". Found during #3475.

Why #3475 did not fix it: the fit of a pocket depends on the region that the generator cuts. That region depends on the containment (an open side lets a wider tool cut from outside), the stock and the part slice (`operation::selection_region`, `pocket_region_memo`, area controls). The command does not have that region without these steps. A bounding-box or width estimate can refuse legal work, so #3475 added none.

Also owed (same rule, other doors):
- `EditOperationParams`: an edit of a plain Slot's `width` or `stock_to_leave` that makes the current tool too wide is not refused at the command. #3475 refuses only at create, at `set_tool` (`EditOperationLinks`) and at a `ChangeTool` that widens the tool. The shared rule is `camcraft_motion::machining2d::slot_centre_band` and the sentence is `operation::tool_gate::slot_fit_refusal`.

Expected: an accepted pocket edit with a named `warning` in the MCP reply (the `clearance_warning` pattern of `edit_operation`), and the same text in the UI, when the generator's own predicate (`non_sliver_center(region, r + stock_to_leave)` is empty) says that the tool cannot fit. The check must use the same region as generate, or it must not run.

Done means: a pinning test shows the warning for a too-wide tool on a closed Inside pocket, and no warning for an Outside pocket that the generator cuts; a Slot width edit below the tool is refused at the command with the #3475 sentence.

title: No way to open a project read-only: Save can write over a reference copy

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**What happened**

CamCraft cannot open a project read-only. Every open project saves over its own file:

- In the window, Save writes to the file that was opened (`crates/ui/src/state.rs:3436-3440` on `main` 60b19abe8).
- The MCP tool `save_project` without a path, and the script call `cam.save()`, write to the file that was opened (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs:41-52`).
- `camcraft-ui` has no read-only option. `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` stops with `unknown option '--read-only'` (`crates/ui/src/cli_options.rs:192`).
- The MCP tool `open_project` takes only `path`. `open_project {"path": "job.camproj", "read_only": true}` is refused with `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:115-123`).

These users need a project that opens without a risk to its file:

- a user who opens a shipped example or a tester kit to look at it;
- a person who reviews a released job;
- a team that keeps reference copies on a shared folder.

CamCraft already has this behaviour for shipped machines. The machine editor refuses Save for a shipped machine, and Save As writes a copy (`crates/app/src/machine/draft.rs:35-36`, `:229-242`, `:259`).

**Expected**

- `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only.
- A save over the opened file is refused on every save route: the window, MCP `save_project` and script `cam.save`. The file stays byte for byte.
- Save As to another file works, and the project is then no longer read-only.
- The title bar says that the project is read-only.
- An agent can open a project read-only with `open_project {"path": ..., "read_only": true}`.

An open SolidCraft pull request adds the same option, `solidcraft --read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830). The same name and behaviour in both apps help users who use the two.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Copy a project file, for example a shipped example, to a folder.
2. Run `camcraft-ui --read-only <copy>.camproj`. The start stops with `unknown option '--read-only'`.
3. Run `camcraft-ui <copy>.camproj`. Change a parameter and push Save. CamCraft writes over the copy.
4. In `camcraft-cli mcp`, call `open_project {"path": "<copy>.camproj", "read_only": true}`. The call is refused: `open_project: unknown argument "read_only"`.

I found this by code inspection.

**camcraft version and OS**

`main` at 60b19abe8 (2026-11-22). Windows 11.

**Proposed change**

- A new start option `--read-only` in the option table (`cli_options.rs`). It applies to the one project file on the command line. A model file is imported as usual, because an import makes a new project with no file. A headless start ignores it.
- One rule in `crates/app/src/project/`, `project::refuse_read_only_save`, next to `project::save` and its other refusals. It refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The window's `save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it. `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP seam of a window.
- The rule compares files, not spellings (canonical paths), because the Save As dialog gives an absolute path.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as the shipped-machine editor does. A save to the opened file from the dialog is refused on the status line.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- MCP `open_project` gets an optional `read_only` boolean. Scripts get it through `cam.call("open_project", ...)`. The live seam still refuses `open_project`, but the window's read-only state reaches a live `save_project`.
- The title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.
- No file-format change. `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change.

**Done means:** `camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens the project read-only and the title says so. Tests show that a save over the opened file is refused, and that the file stays byte for byte, through the window, MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live seam. Tests show that a save to another file works and ends read-only. A test shows that the option parses and keeps the file argument. The help text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`, the site guide and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` describe it.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Face with 'Do not touch': blocked lower levels leave the face above Cut Z, and only a note says so

body:
Found in the second read of PR #3413 (head b38f0c12f). The label `bug` applies.

## What happens
A Face operation with protected items clips its rows by a keep-out. The keep-out of a level covers the heights from that level up to the clearance plane. A lower level gets the same keep-out or a larger one. Thus the blocked levels are always the lowest levels.

When one or more levels are blocked and one level stays clear, the operation generates. The face can stop above Cut Z in each place. The only sign is the note "blocked N facing level(s); the remaining levels stayed clear" (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_keep.rs:425-429`).

The note does not say that Cut Z was not reached. Nothing marks the operation "incomplete". The Prime Directive says: "If an operation can only be computed in part, mark it 'incomplete'."

The result is not a gouge. Material stays that the user expects to be removed.

## Wanted
- When a blocked level leaves the face above Cut Z, the operation says so in plain English with the depth that it reached, and it is marked "incomplete" (or refused: record the decision).
- A test with a keep-out that changes with Z (an item that is wider at a lower level) pins the message and the state.

title: Verifier: a rapid that the part-solid law convicts says "travels through stock (below the clearance plane)"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the bounded search of #3319 (2026-11-22).

## What happens

The part-solid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs:214-237`) judges each rapid against the part solid. When the tool body or its edge column meets the part, it pushes `Warning::RapidInStock { at: i }`.

That warning prints this text (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs:467-468`):

`rapid move N travels through stock (below the clearance plane, or at it below the stock top)`

The text is wrong for this case:
- The rapid can be vertical (a lift out of a pass, or a drop to a pass start).
- The rapid can be at or above the clearance plane at one end.
- The tool meets the part, not the uncut stock.

The user then reads it as a lateral G0 under the clearance plane. This is what happened in #3319.

## How to see it

Headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`, on `origin/main` 835556814 and on v0.25.0 (7e2a8119c):
1. `import_model` `testdata/models/fig8.step`; `add_tool` `EM-0800-4FL`; `fit_stock` box, sides `[5,5,5,5,0,2]`.
2. `edit_tool` `{"flute_len": 10}`.
3. `add_operation` "2D Offset" on the bottom face (Z 0), containment Outside. Clearance = Top of stock +10, Top = Top of stock +0, Bottom = Selection +1.5, Stepdown 10, Entry Helix r 1.6, `retract_z` null.
4. `generate`, then `verify`.

Result: `shank_hit` on moves 1406-1658 and 2194-2446 (the outer ring of levels 2 and 3), and `rapid_in_stock` on moves 1659, 2193 and 2447. Moves 1659 and 2447 are the vertical lifts to Z 32 at (-0.202, -33.998). Move 2193 is the vertical drop to Z 4 at the same point. Each lateral G0 of the posted program (a long-flute copy of the same path) is at Z 32.

The post is blocked, so the output is safe. Only the message is wrong.

## Done means

- A rapid that the part-solid law convicts gets a message that says the tool meets the part on a rapid, and that names the move.
- `rapids.rs` keeps its text for a rapid through the stock.
- A pin test in `crates/sim/tests/` shows the two texts on the two cases.
- The MCP `kind` string and the UI severity stay correct for the new text.

Bracket 200 x 120 x 6 mild steel: Ø40 hole, two 12 x 30 slots, four Ø10 holes. Plasma Profile, holes first, outer last. `verify` answers:

"findings": [],
"gate": {"ok": true, "problems": [],

The plasma laws did judge the program and found 4 tip-up crossings (the torch rapids over slugs that are already cut free and may have tipped up), but the only place they appear is a sentence inside `not_judged`. body:
Found by the QA swarm round 2 (#2582): four of the five agent runs on CamCraft **v0.25.0** (Linux x86_64 release, headless MCP) lost time or a feature to this.

## What happens

`list_operation_types` prints each kind's fields with defaults and one note: "Fields absent from the defaults are optional and off; set them in a params patch to turn them on." It never names those fields. In v0.25.0:

| kind | fields listed | accepted but not listed (found by the agents through serde errors or not at all) |
|---|---|---|
| pocket, face, contour, ... | pocket: bottom_z, clearance_z, climb, entry, feed, helix_radius, optimal_load, plunge_feed, stepdown, stepover, stock_to_leave, strategy, top_z | `tilt` (the 3+1 / 3+2 index, guide "Indexed work"), `rest` (RestDto: previous_tool_diameter, ...) |
| wire_contour | bottom_z, side, top_z | `condition` (**required**: add_operation refuses without it), `taper_deg`, `start`, `skims`, `tabs` {count, width, at, cutoff_condition}, `capture` |
| plasma_profile | bottom_z, clearance_z, comp, lead_in, lead_out, overburn, reversed, small_hole_dia, small_hole_feed, top_z | `feed`, `kerf`, `pierce_delay`, `pierce_height`, `cut_height` (unset, the posted plasma program had no F word and no M207/M208/M209) |
| drill | ... cycle ... | `cross` (see #3448); `cycle`'s values (auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream, fine_bore) |

Enum fields (`cycle`, `strategy`, `entry`, `side`, finish3d `pattern`) are typed only `"string"`.

Effect seen in the runs: q05 never found `tilt`, so it programmed the 4th-axis faces as manual re-clamp setups instead of indexed A moves; q06 had to probe `condition`, `taper_deg`, `capture` and the plasma feed/pierce fields one error at a time; q04 found `rest` only from a serde error.

## Expected

Each kind lists every field it accepts (with type, unit, default or "off", and the allowed values of an enum), so an agent can discover a feature from the tool alone. #3217 covers the wire-only part of this and the camcraft-mcp skill.

## Evidence

Agent reports: [q05 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q05-4axis/REPORT.md) (confusing-tools 4), [q06 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q06-wire-plasma/REPORT.md) problem 2, [q04 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q04-vcarve-sign/REPORT.md) problem 4, [q01 REPORT.md](https://github.com/mkinney/Camcraft/blob/qa-artifacts/qa/round2-20261122/q01-2d-plate/REPORT.md) (enum values).

Done means: list_operation_types names every accepted field of every kind, optional ones marked as such, with enum values listed; a test fails when a params struct gains a field the listing does not show.
