body:
## What happens

Found while working #3300. The 5-axis stamp (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`) gives the approach feed the lean of its end station. The approach feed starts upright at the clearance and ends at the first contact. So the rotaries turn during the descent to the stock.

Posted on `assets/machines/tilthead.mch` with `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` (the #3300 case, 5-Axis Contour on a spherical cap, clearance 20 mm, G54 at Z 50):

```text
G43.4 H01
G00 Z-30.
G00 X0. Y-3.84 Z-30. A0. B0.
G01 X-0.776 Y-3.149 Z-47.314 A13.313 B15.42 F100
```

The G01 block turns A by 13.3 degrees and B by 15.4 degrees while the tool moves 17 mm down to the part. Flow5D and Swarf show the same opening (A21.6 B9.8, and A32.5 B17.9).

This is not new with #3300. On a machine with no stated rotary rate, main posts the same G01 block today. #3300 only makes the start angle known (A0 B0 at the clearance).

## Expected

The rotaries go to the first lean at a safe height, then the tool approaches the part with a constant pose: retract, rotate, then approach. A rotary move near the stock is the exception, and a judgment states why it is safe.

## Notes

- `cam.verify()` passes this program. It is not proven that the turn gouges. This issue asks for a decision on the approach law.
- A fix changes the stamp's pose law for the approach stations (a held lead-in pose, or a rapid that turns at the clearance). It changes posted G-code, so the safety floor applies.

Done means: the opening approach of a leaning 5-axis path does not turn a rotary below the clearance, or a decision records why the current law is safe. A test pins the chosen law with the tilt-head machine.

title: Windows: camcraft-ui lib test binary crashes (STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION) with 12 test threads; passes single-threaded

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:ui

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
### What happens

On two Windows 11 machines (bacon: Intel NUC with iGPU; lenny: desktop), the Windows quick check of `main` is red on one step:

```
FAIL  ui suites: lib  exit 101
process didn't exit successfully: `...\camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=12` (exit code: 0xc0000005, STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION)
```

The binary dies after about 100 tests with a native access violation, not a failed assert. Last tests printed before the crash (bacon, main `7a626a7f5`): the `egui_app::setup_plane_tests` / `setup_points_tests` group.

### It is a concurrency crash

The same binary, same tree, run single-threaded on bacon:

```
camcraft_ui-b30d80154151484e.exe --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 1425 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored; finished in 166.04s
```

Linux (len, post-merge runners) and macOS (m3) are green on the same commits. Likely candidates: tests that create a graphics device/adapter (wgpu) or another thread-unsafe native resource in parallel. Related but different: #3258 (several UI binaries on one Linux host, fixed by #3302 naming the crash status); this one is one binary, several test threads, on Windows.

### Workaround

`--test-threads=1` for `camcraft-ui --lib` on Windows (the gate stays slower but green).

**Done means:** `cargo xtask gate quick` on Windows runs `ui suites: lib` green at its normal thread count, or the gate serialises exactly the tests that share the native resource, with a test or gate-plan pin and the crashing resource named in the decision note.

**Triage.** P3: a red gate on Windows only, with a workaround; no wrong output. `effort:medium`: test harness / gate plan, one crate.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> issue; enhancement; support for tapered tooling like ball mills, roundover bits and similar, router style tooling.

Part of #3351. Refs #3351. Sub-issue 3 of the plan in #3351.

Depends on #3367

## What to do

Add one milling kind for a form cutter. Its meridian is the drawn outline. This is slice 1 of #896 for the tool data, without the undercut forms.

1. `ToolKind::FormMill` with the file word `form_mill` in `ToolKindDto` and `KindWord` (additive, no version step). `ToolKind::Form` stays the lathe form gauge.
2. A `FormMill` must carry a valid outline in the existing `ToolDto::cutter` field (`SpunProfile`). `Tool::meridian()` (#3367) reads it. `cutter_fit::refit` keeps the drawn flute points of a `FormMill` and does not overwrite them from `Tool::profile`. `tool_cutter::digest` hashes the whole cutting outline of a `FormMill`.
3. An optional pilot band at the tip: a non-cutting band with its own radius (a bearing).
4. Presets that write the outline from their numbers, with the terms of public router bit catalogues:
   - roundover (corner rounding): radius, pilot radius, cutting height;
   - cove: radius, cutting height;
   - ogee: the two radii and the step;
   - V-groove: included angle, tip radius;
   - bead.
5. In this issue, `FormMill` accepts only a non-decreasing meridian (no undercut). An undercut outline is refused by name and stays in #896.
6. The tool dialog: the kind in the type list, a preset list with its number rows, and the Profile tab for a drawn outline. The change goes through `ChangeTool` / `AddTool`.
7. MCP: `add_tool`, `edit_tool` and the cutter tools take the kind, the preset and its numbers.
8. `FormMill` is in the 2D Chamfer family (`tool_law.rs`) so that `no_orphan_tool_kinds` stays green. The 2D Chamfer generator door refuses it by name until the edge form sub-issue opens it.
9. Catalogue: one roundover, one cove and one V-groove bit, in mm and inch, with numbers from public maker catalogues.

## Rules

- `effort:high`: several crates, new behaviour with its tests. No toolpath changes: the doors refuse.
- Shapes and terms come from public tool catalogues and handbooks. No HSMWorks material.

## Done means

- Each preset gives a valid outline and a meridian whose cutting radius matches its catalogue numbers (pinned).
- A `FormMill` round-trips through the project file, the library file and MCP, and keeps its drawn outline after a number edit.
- Each operation refuses a `FormMill` by name, and 2D Chamfer names the edge form work.
- The dialog test asserts the kind, the preset list and the Profile tab.

## What to do

This is slice 1, slice 5 and slice 6 of the research in #895. That research is the specification: the fields, the tip math (`r_flat`, `r_t`, `z_t`, `r0`) and the sane rules.

1. `Tool` gets `tip_diameter` (default 0) and `tip_form` (`Sharp`, `Flat`, `Ball`; default `Sharp`). `corner_r` is the tip or corner radius of a `Taper`. The taper math goes in a new module (for example `crates/tools/src/taper.rs`).
2. `Tool::meridian()` (#3367) and `Tool::profile` read the real tip.
3. `ToolDto` (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs`) and the catalogue `Def` (`crates/tools/src/catalog_asset.rs`) get the two fields as `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = ...)]`. Old files and `assets/tools/catalog.json` load as `Sharp`. No version step (the additive rule of `file.rs`).
4. The tool dialog shows a tip form row and a tip diameter for `Taper`. It clears the stale tip fields when the kind changes. The change goes through `ChangeTool` / `AddTool` (one undo step).
5. MCP: `set_tool_cutter_params`, `add_tool` and `edit_tool` (`crates/app/src/mcp/cutter_tools.rs`) take `tip_diameter` and `tip_form`.
6. Catalogue: add one tapered flat end mill, one tapered ball nose and one flat-tip chamfer bit, with numbers from public maker catalogues.
7. Each operation door refuses a non-sharp `Taper` by name ("the tip form is not read by this operation yet"). This keeps the toolpaths of today. The doors open in the consumer sub-issues.

## Rules

- `effort:high`: several crates (tools, app, ui, MCP), new behaviour with its tests. No toolpath changes: the doors refuse.
- The tip form is a user parameter with a default (`Sharp`). It is not a second kind.

## Done means

- A tapered flat, a tapered ball nose and a flat-tip chamfer bit pass `is_sane` and round-trip through the project file, the library file and MCP.
- A sharp `Taper` keeps the same profile, digest and stamp as before (pinned).
- Each operation refuses a non-sharp `Taper` by name (pinned in `crates/app/tests/tool_law.rs`).
- The dialog test asserts the tip form row, its labels and its enabled state.

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The "Do not touch" group of the Geometry tab (Boundaries) does not work on a 2D Pocket operation. The group shows only the note "'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far". There is no "Pick protected" button. The maintainer asked for "do not touch" on operations, in his words: "the calculation should avoid to gouge them at all costs" (#2055).

Found during the work on #3335. Refs #2055. Refs #3335.

## What to do

1. Add `OpType::Pocket` to `do_not_touch_applies` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`).
2. Make the 2D Pocket generator keep the full tool (flutes, shank and holder) clear of each protected face and edge, by the clearance. This includes the cutting moves, the lead moves, the link moves and the plunges.
3. If the generator cannot keep clear, refuse the operation or mark it "incomplete". The diagnostic names the item. The post is blocked.
4. The verify check and the post gate already check the protected items. Make sure that they read the 2D Pocket moves.

## Safety

This work is under the safety floor: it changes the toolpath and the posted G-code of a 2D Pocket operation that has protected items. A 2D Pocket operation without protected items must give the same toolpath as before. Pin that.

## Done means

- The Boundary group of a 2D Pocket operation shows "Pick protected", and a viewport click adds a face or an edge row.
- A test with a protected face next to the cut shows that no move comes nearer than the clearance.
- A test with a protected face that the cut cannot avoid shows the refusal with the item named, and a blocked post.
- A test shows that a 2D Pocket operation without protected items gives the same toolpath.

body:
Refs #1448. Part of #1448. Follow-up of #3324.

## Why

The design of #3324 (`docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-shared.md`, section 2) chooses an operation-level project key for the start and exit picks. The PR of #3324 does not move the storage. The move puts one field on every path variant of `OpParams` and its DTO. More than ten open PRs change `wire_edm.rs` and `wire_edm_dto.rs`, so the move in the same PR conflicts with all of them.

The accessor `OpParams::path_picks()` hides the storage, so the family slices of #1448 that have a `links` field do not wait for this issue.

## What to do

- Store `camcraft_motion::path_picks::PathPicks` on every path kind.
- Write the key `picks: { start: [[x, y, z?], ...], exit: [...] }` at the operation level. Write it only when a list is not empty.
- Read the old keys on load: `links.approach.start_point`, `links.approach.exit_point` and the wire `start`.
- Keep the digest bytes `0xC7` / `0xC8` for the same values. No contour golden changes.
- Move `Approach::start_point` / `exit_point` and `WireContourOp.start` into the new field. Change `start_exit_rows.rs`, `start_exit_pick.rs` and the contour planner to read `path_picks()`.

## Done means

- A load test opens a file with the old `links.approach.start_point` key and a file with the old wire `start` key. The picks are the same after the load.
- Every contour golden and every contour pick test stays green with no change.
- This merges before the first family slice of #1448 for a kind with no `links` field (Face, turning, plasma).

title: Performance: the stock simulation is very slow - it runs on the CPU, the GPU shader path is not built

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; performance; P2; the stock simulation; is extremly slow. This was supposed to be calculated on the GPU as a shader, it doesnt seem to be the case..

## What the repository shows

The maintainer is right: the stock removal does not run on the GPU. The plan exists. It is built only in part.

- #2607 (research, closed) decided: "The GPU does the display playback cut. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict. The home for GPU compute code is `camcraft-gpu` (#2620)." It made the slices S1 to S6.
- S1 #2626 (the CPU f32 twin of the cell cut kernel) is merged. It is a CPU twin, by design. It runs no shader.
- #2620 (the `camcraft-gpu` compute crate: probe, cached device, CPU fallback) is NOT merged. Its work is held on the pushed branch `issue/2620-gpu-compute-seam` at `90c98be93`, since 2026-11-19 (the gate stopped for disk space). Its label is `claimed`, P4.
- S2 #2627 (the WGSL removal kernel for ball and flat tools, linear moves), S3 #2629 (viewport playback on the GPU, with CPU fallback), S4 #2628, S5 #2630 and S6 #2631 are open at P4. S3 to S6 are `blocked`.
- So the playback in the viewport still uses the CPU engines. A long program is slow.

## What the maintainer needs

The Simulate view plays a program at a usable speed, with a visible stock cut. The frame target is under 10 ms for a still frame (`docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`).

## Plan

1. Measure first. A scout and a worker time the playback on a real program (the `fig8` 2D Offset, EM-0800-4FL, and one 3D Pocket). The numbers go in a comment: cells, moves, milliseconds for each frame and for the cut. This shows where the time goes: the cut, the mesh, the upload, or the frame.
2. Quick wins on the CPU path that the measure shows, if any. Each has a counter test (AGENTS.md "Frame cost").
3. Finish the GPU path in order: #2620, then #2627 (S2), then #2629 (S3). Raise their priority to P2 and the type to bug (they are the fix of this issue). S4, S5 and S6 stay P4 and follow.
4. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict (the verify check, the collision check, the post gate). The GPU result is display only. A machine without a usable GPU falls back to the CPU path and says so.

## Safety

The simulation that blocks the post is not changed by this work. Any change to the f64 engines is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- A recorded measure before and after, in a comment.
- On the reference machine, the Simulate view of a `fig8` program plays at a usable frame rate.
- A counter test: a still frame cuts nothing again.
- A CPU fallback test for a machine without a GPU.

- Start: the raster begins at the corner of the face region nearest the pick. The row direction and the step direction follow from that corner.
- Exit: the last row ends at the side nearest the exit pick. If the row count and the start corner make that impossible, the exit is refused by name.
- Holes that bound the rows (`face_holes.rs`) keep their law.

Seam: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face.rs:119` (`face`), `:129` (`face_led`), `:146` (`face_over`).

## Why effort:max

The raster order and the row direction come from a new planning rule (start corner, step direction, exit side). This is a toolpath algorithm change.

## Laws a pick must keep (refused by name, never moved)

- The first traverse (`operation/first_traverse.rs:45`).
- The lead and the overrun of each row stay outside the part.
- An exit that the row count cannot reach is refused.

## Done means

- A pin test for each of the four start corners, with golden CL.
- A pin test for an exit side, and one for an impossible exit refused by name.
- Undo and redo restore the previous path. MCP `edit_operation` sets the picks.
- Every shipped Face golden without a pick is byte-identical.

Safety floor: this changes toolpaths and posted G-code.

Research only: no code, no branch, no PR, no lane slot (AGENTS.md "needs-research is research, not code").

## Why
CamCraft ships 48 machine files (`assets/machines/*.mch`), but the simulation shows each machine as simple blocks and cylinders (#2584). Many machine makers publish real 3D models of their machines, so the posed machine could look like the actual machine.

## Questions to answer (in comments on this issue)
1. **Which machines have a public 3D model?** For each `.mch` file, list: the maker's page, the format (STEP, Parasolid, IGES, STL...), whether the model is split into moving parts (table, saddle, head, spindle, rotary axes) or is one solid, its size, and the **licence or terms of use**.
   Machines: 3axis-vmc, agiecut-classic-2s, doosan-dnm(-3axis), fehlmann-picomax55, grbl-3axis, grblhal-3axis, haas-dm1, haas-dt1, haas-mini-mill, haas-vf2, haas-vf2ss, lathe, linuxcnc-3axis, makera-carvera(-air), makera-z1, millturn, sienci-altmill-2x4/4x4/4x8, sinker-edm, sodick-alc400g, tilthead, tinyg-3axis, the Tormach range (440, 770/770M/770M+/770MX/-ML/microarc4, 1100 S1-S3/M/M+/MX, 1300PL, 1500MX, 8L, 15L/15LX Slant-Pro, 24R, xsTECH/Pro), vmc. Generic files (vmc, 3axis-vmc, lathe, millturn, tilthead, the grbl/tinyg/linuxcnc ones) need no vendor model; say so.
2. **Download** each model that may be downloaded for local use into `~/m5data/machine-cad/<machine>/` on M5, with a `SOURCE.md` per machine: the URL, the date, the licence text or a link to it, and the file's sha256. **Never commit them to this repo or rehost them anywhere** unless the licence clearly allows redistribution. Do not download anything behind a login or sign-up form; list it as "needs a human" instead.
3. **Can CamCraft show them?** Check each model against what the sim view needs:
   - Can its parts be mapped to the `.mch` axis tree (which part moves with X, Y, Z, A, B, C)?
   - How many triangles does each part have after meshing at display resolution? Is decimation needed?
   - Where is its origin compared with the `.mch` machine zero?
4. **Where it should live.** Pick one, with the reasons:
   - (a) in CamCraft: a STEP or mesh body per part in the `.mch` file (#2591), loaded from a path the user supplies, since the model itself is not ours to ship;
   - (b) a side project: a fetch script plus per-machine part maps in `mkinney/cam-tools-and-fixtures` (the same pattern as its vendor fixture fetch), which CamCraft reads when present;
   - (c) URDF assemblies (#2593), for example built in SolidCraft from the vendor STEP.

## Clean-room limits
Use machine makers' own public downloads only. **No models from Autodesk, Fusion, HSMWorks or any other CAM vendor's machine library**, and nothing taken from another CAM product's install.

## Done means
- One comment per machine family with the table from question 1.
- The models that may be downloaded are in `~/m5data/machine-cad/`, each with its `SOURCE.md`.
- A recorded decision on (a), (b) or (c).
- The concrete sub-issues for that decision are filed, each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, "Part of #this" and a "Done means" line. This issue is then closed.

Related: #2584 (simple machine model), #2591 (STEP body in .mch), #2593 (machine from URDF), #2587 (sim view).

title: 2D Chamfer: select a tip offset

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Wanted

A 2D Chamfer can state a tip offset. The cone then cuts the requested chamfer through a radial band above that radius.

This lets the user keep the selected edge and the requested chamfer width. For example, a 6 mm chamfer mill can cut a 1 mm chamfer at a 2 mm tip offset. The cutting band is then 2 mm to 3 mm from the tool axis.

## Current behaviour

CamCraft places the virtual cone tip on the selected wall. It keeps the tip at:

```text
tip_z = top_z - width * tan(angle)
```

The tool centre has no XY offset from the picked line. A larger chamfer mill therefore cuts through the smallest part of its cone. The operation has no setting that moves to a larger-radius band of the same cone.

## Proposed rule

For an ideal sharp cone, add one operation value named `Tip offset`.

```text
tip offset = r
chamfer width = w
centreline offset toward air = r
tip_z = top_z - (r + w) * tan(chamfer angle)
contact radius = r to r + w
```

For a 45-degree chamfer, a 6 mm tool, `w = 1 mm`, and `r = 2 mm`:

```text
centreline offset = 2 mm
contact radius = 2 mm to 3 mm
tip_z = top_z - 3 mm
```

The final chamfer stays 1 mm wide. The tool uses a 2 mm to 3 mm part of the cone instead of its 0 mm to 1 mm part.

The `Side` setting determines the air side for closed rings and selected open chains.

## Safety doors

- Refuse when `r` is negative or not finite.
- Refuse when the tool radius is smaller than `r + width`.
- Refuse when the cone or flute reach cannot supply `(r + width) * tan(angle)`.
- Offset closed loops and open chains with the same air-side law.
- Refuse an offset that folds, disappears, or reaches material on the air side.
- Keep the declared `EdgeBreak` on the original picked edge with the authored width and depth. The larger contact band must not create credit for more edge work.
- Stock simulation and collision verification must judge the offset cone position, not the old tip-on-wall position.

## Scope

This issue does not model or compensate for tool-tip wear. It selects a band of the current ideal sharp cone.

Issue #895 is related because it tracks real flat, ball, and radiused tip geometry. This operation-level feature can be specified independently.

## Done means

- The Geometry page exposes `Tip offset` for a 2D Chamfer.
- The value round-trips through project files and the MCP operation parameter surface.
- A 45-degree, 6 mm ideal cone cuts an authored 1 mm chamfer with a 2 mm tip offset.
- A test proves the contact radii are 2 mm and 3 mm, and the tip path is 3 mm below the top plane.
- A motion test proves a closed ring offsets toward the side `Side` names.
- A motion test proves each selected open chain offsets toward its air side.
- The tool-radius and flute-reach refusals name the missing dimension.
- Stock simulation proves the final 1 mm edge break and no gouge on the part.
- Existing 0 mm tip offset projects keep the current path byte for byte.

## Labels

Suggested triage: `enhancement`, `area:2d`, `P6`, and `effort:high`.

Changelog: A 2D Chamfer can use a selected larger-radius band of a chamfer mill while preserving the authored chamfer width.

## What happens

The user cannot chamfer one edge or one section of a solid edge loop without cutting the complete loop.

## Expected

- The Geometry section accepts one or more open edge chains for a 2D Chamfer.
- Each chain is cut only from its first selected point to its last selected point.
- Closed face and loop picks keep the current closed-circuit behaviour.
- The tool enters and leaves each open chain safely.

title: Bore: a helical strategy (continuous helix to full depth, then a floor circle)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
### What are you trying to do

Counterbores for M6 cap screws in aluminium: Ø11 × 7 deep, cut with a Ø6 flat end mill on a small 3-axis mill (LinuxCNC, ER20 spindle). The usual way to cut these is helical interpolation: the tool spirals down on the wall radius to full depth, then runs one flat circle at the floor. It never plunges straight into solid material.

In 0.24.0 the Bore operation is a level-by-level ring ladder. At each step-down level the tool dives at the hole centre, sweeps out to the wall and runs a ring, then moves to the next level. The source describes the first engagement as the bore's centre dive, and the Lead-in tab has no entry choice for Bore. Linking → Level to level → Helix helps between levels, but that helix runs on a 1 mm radius at the centre and the first dive is still a plunge. With a 1 mm step-down that comes to 7 plunges and 7 rings per counterbore.

On a light machine, a flat end mill plunging into solid aluminium is the move most likely to chatter, pack chips or snap the tool. That's why the helical cycle is the default for counterbores and holes bored with an end mill.

### How you imagine it working

A **Helical** strategy in the Bore operation (or a separate Helical bore operation):

- The tool positions over the hole at the retract plane and descends on a **continuous helix** whose radius puts the cutter's rim on the finished wall (hole radius − tool radius − stock to leave), from Top Z to the hole floor.
- **Helix pitch** (mm per turn) is set by the user, with a sensible automatic value. Alternatively a maximum ramp angle.
- At the floor, **one full flat circle** to remove the ramp step, then a move off the wall towards the centre before retracting.
- Optional **spring pass**: a second floor circle with no extra depth.
- **Climb or conventional**, as Bore has now.
- For holes too wide for one helix to clear the core (wider than about 2 × tool diameter): helix at an inner radius first, then step out in rings at the floor, or simply refuse with a clear message.
- **Through holes:** continue the helix past the floor by the break-through allowance.

The rest of Bore can stay as it is (hole detection, per-hole floors, the reach checks).

Happy to test builds on the counterbore case above and air-cut the result on my machine.

title: 3D Finish: an option to stop the waterline ring pass on steep flanks

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## What is asked

A contributor asks for one control on 3D Finish: a switch that turns off the waterline ring pass, so the operation cuts its raster lines only. The contributor's words, quoted unchanged (chat, 2026-11-19):

> how hard would it be to make a checkbox that can disable the waterline portion?

## What the tool does today

A Parallel 3D Finish operation splits the terrain at 45 degrees. Shallow facets get the Z-following raster lines. Steep facets get waterline rings: `parallel()` runs one raster pass, then `rings_and_tail` (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` line 210). The ring paths run about 90 degrees across the raster lines. Every wall that stands above the Bottom plane gets its ring ladder: hole walls, end walls, and the sloped edges of a tilted top face.

The picture below shows a contributor's test part: a long bar with a top face tilted 2 degrees and two openings, cut with a 0.3125 in ball-end, Bottom 0.300 in. The purple arrow marks one ring run that still survives on a wall near the near end. The tall ladders at the far end wall are the same law at the high end of the sloped face. The raster family cannot cover those walls; only the rings can.

![Ring run surviving on a wall at Bottom 0.300 in, parallel to the bar length and near the near end edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/screenshots/issue-2811-waterline-arrow.png)

## Why the switch is wanted

On a part whose steep flanks are out of scope, the rings add cutting time, and they add paths the machinist did not ask for. Some machinists want the lines only, and accept the walls as they stand. One checkbox should say that choice out loud.

## Proposed shape

- One parameter, for example `waterlines: bool`, default on. Existing behaviour does not change.
- GUI name: not just "off". The control must name the consequence, for example "Steep flanks: Waterlines / Leave uncut".
- The switch applies to the Parallel pattern. Whether Parallel multi and Scallop take it is a decision. Blend should likely never take it: its 30-45 degree double cut needs the rings to remove the staircase (its own note says so). The maintainer decides this scope.

## Laws the switch must keep

1. With the switch off and steep flanks present, the path must carry a visible note that names the uncut flanks and their count. Silent rest material is not allowed (Prime Directive).
2. A model that is fully steep with the switch off must refuse with a clear error, not post an empty program. The raster answers `false` for an all-steep model; today "the rings alone carry it".
3. The parameter round-trips in the project file. Old project files load with the default, on.
4. The 3D finish MCP parameter surface exposes the same field (same rule as `fill_openings` and `gap_link`).

## Measured support (headless probe, main `744c0847b`)

Synthetic model: bar 24 x 160 mm, flat bottom z 0, top face sloped 2 degrees, two through openings, ball 7.94 mm, Parallel, gap link Jump. The probe classifies the XY direction of every Feed move.

- Bottom 0: 188 along-wall Y-family Feed runs at Z ladder levels about 0.4 mm apart. Zero Feed runs cross the open top face. All perpendicular feed sits on walls.
- Bottom raised to 9.75 mm (near the high top edge): the same perpendicular runs collapse to three ladder levels per wall, and only over the stretch where the face still stands above Bottom. Nothing sits in the open middle.

This matches the picture: raising Bottom shrank the ring set everywhere except where walls still rise above it. The behaviour is correct as designed; this issue asks for control, not for a defect fix. The probe code can become the pinning test for the switch.

## Done means

- A checkbox flips the ring pass on and off, and each state has a motion test that pins it.
- Off plus steep flanks: a note names the uncut flanks; no ring moves appear in the CL output.
- Off plus a steep-only model: a refusal with a clear message.
- Project-file round-trip test and MCP parity pass.
- The 3D finish page shows the control with its consequence wording.

## Classification

This account is a contributor and cannot set labels. Suggested labels, for a maintainer: `enhancement`, `P6`, `effort:high` (safety floor: it changes posted G-code when the switch is used), `area:motion`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp`. The body was written by the contributor's agent at the contributor's request.

body: ### What are you trying to do I want to describe my own machine in the Machines pane, for example a 3-axis grblHAL mill with a 4th-axis rotary (A, about X) on the table. The file editor (machine_file_editor.rs) shows one field for each key the file already has (machine::fields). It cannot add an axis, remove one or change their order in kinematics.default.parts. Today I have to edit the .mch file in a text editor and reload it. ### How you imagine it working - One row per axis part, in chain order, under `table` or under `head` in `kinematics.default.parts`, with up, down and remove buttons and an "add axis" control. A linear part is `X`, `Y`, `Z` (and `U`, `V` for a wire machine); a rotary part is `A`, `B` or `C`. - A linear row edits `direction` (`1` / `-1`, #373). - A rotary row edits `axis` (±X, ±Y, ±Z, or three numbers for any other vector) and its travel, or none for continuous. - A rotary that turns the work also edits `nose_to_axis` and `axis_to_table` (#785), the two distances the clearance gates read. They are measurable with a rule or taken from the maker's data. - Under them, a collapsed "Kinematics" group holds `pivot` and `offset` (#1962). It is closed by default and open when the file already states a pivot. For a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head), the group is open instead, since the two distances do not apply to it and the pivot is what places it. This issue only adds the group; #1970's rows fill it (see below). - The letter follows the `axis` by RS-274: about X is `A`, about Y is `B`, about Z is `C`. When `axis` is set, the editor suggests that letter. A row whose letter and `axis` disagree (an `A` about Y, say) shows a note at the row; whether that should also block a save is the validator's call, as now. - The edits go through `MachineDraft`, as `add_coolant` and `remove_coolant` do, so keys the editor does not know are kept. - The validator judges the result as now. A refusal shows at the row it concerns, and a save stays blocked while a refusal stands. - Moving a rotary changes its `parent` and `chain_order`, since the parser derives them from the nesting (#1962). Tests pin that, and that `pivot`, `offset`, `zero_offset`, `rollover` and `sign_convention` survive an add, a move and a remove. For illustration only, the axis list as it started to look in another CAM tool (solidcraft). It is a hint at the idea, not a layout to copy. Its `Pivot` row stands in the open; the proposal here puts the pivot in a collapsed group instead. **Overlap with #1970.** #1970 adds rows for the #1962 trunnion keys to `fields.rs` and `sheet.rs`, the same files and the same rotary row. This issue does not edit those keys; it only keeps them, and the rotary row's collapsed "Kinematics" group is where #1970's rows go. Its blockers (#1962, #1965, #1968) look done on `main`, so the two may run at the same time. Should this one wait for #1970, go first, or be folded into it? **A question before any code.** A rotary can be placed by `nose_to_axis` / `axis_to_table` (#785) or by `pivot` / `offset` (#1962). I do not see them as alternatives: the clearance gates read the #785 pair, the post's kinematics the #1962 pair, so a file may well want both. Hence the proposal above rather than a choice between them: a rotary that turns the work shows the two distances, with `pivot` / `offset` in a collapsed group; a rotary under `head` (one that tilts the tool, like a B head) shows the group open, since the two distances do not apply to it. Does that split work for you, or should the editor show both pairs alike? **And one about a machine with both.** `nose_to_axis` is measured with Z at `safe_retract`, and as I read it with the head straight. On a machine with a tilting head (B under `head`) and a rotary that turns the work (A under `table`), the nose moves away from that line as B tilts, so the one number no longer holds. Do the index-swing gates handle such a machine today? If not, should the editor still offer the two distances on its A, or say that they are judged only with the head straight? I would like to take this one if it is wanted.

Create the pure-Rust crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`) beside `crates/post`.
It parses RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556) and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections (`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`) and a 1-based line map.

## Scope
- Depend only on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `thiserror` (no `boa_engine`, no `flecs_ecs`, no `camcraft-post` dependency).
- Record the new `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-geometry` crate edges in `docs/decisions/` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Accept dialect configuration and optional machine reference positions from the caller.
- Track modal groups: motion (`G0`, `G1`, `G2`, `G3`, `G80`), plane (`G17`, `G18`, `G19`), distance (`G90`, `G91`), arc center (`G90.1`, `G91.1`), feed mode (`G94`), units (`G20`, `G21`), length offset (`G43 H`, `G49`), work offsets (`G54`..`G59`), and cycle return (`G98`, `G99`).
- Parse `I`/`J`/`K` arcs and `R` radius arcs (`R > 0` minor arc, `R < 0` major arc) in XY, XZ, and YZ planes.
- Expand canned cycles (`G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G86`, `G89`) into explicit `cl::Move` chains (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs`).
- Handle `T`, `M6`, `S`, `M3`/`M4`/`M5`, `M0`/`M1`/`M2`/`M30`, `G4`, `G61`/`G64`, and `G53`/`G28`/`G30` when reference positions exist.
- Split sections on tool changes and record a 1-based source line number for every move.
- Refuse unknown words, missing unit mode, `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, and `A`/`B`/`C` words by name with the 1-based line number.
- Add a clean-room provenance comment to each module (`AGENTS.md`).

Done means: `camcraft-gcode` builds in the workspace with a `docs/decisions/` entry, parses 3-axis ISO programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections with a 1-based line map, and tests pin modal tracking, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs, canned cycles, unit scaling, and named line-numbered refusals.

title: Import SVG drawings as 2D sketch geometry (paths, shapes, transforms, units), sharing the DXF sketch entity

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P4

body:
**The request (mkinney, 2026-11-15):** "Do we need to handle svg file import?" ... "Yes file it". Many waterjet, laser and plasma users draw in Inkscape or Illustrator and export SVG. WAZER's own app takes SVG and DXF (see #1525).

## What

Import an SVG file as 2D sketch geometry for 2D operations (Contour, Pocket, Engrave/Trace, plasma or waterjet profile). It goes into the same sketch entity as the DXF import, so the operations need no new input path.

## Depends on

- #1860 (DXF core reader), #1861 (2D sketch chaining, outer-vs-hole nesting, open chains) and #1862 (the sketch ECS entity, .camproj persistence, undoable import).
- Stack on those: the SVG reader only produces sketch chains and reuses chaining, nesting and the import command.

## Scope

- **Elements:** `path` (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`. `g` groups with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skew), applied to the geometry.
- **Curves:** cubic and quadratic Béziers and elliptical arcs become arcs or polylines within the document's chord tolerance. An arc stays an arc where it is circular after the transform.
- **Units and scale:** `width`/`height` with units (mm, cm, in, pt, pc, px), and the `viewBox`. px uses 96 px/in (the CSS rule). If the file states no physical size, the import asks for the scale. It never guesses silently.
- **Y axis:** SVG Y points down. Flip it so the drawing appears as it does in the editor.
- **Ignored, with a note:** fill, stroke style, text (unless converted to paths), images, clip paths, masks, `use` references to symbols outside the file.
- **Refusals, by name:** a malformed path, a zero or negative size, a degenerate arc, and a file larger than the import budget give a clear error, never a panic (the Prime Directive).
- **MCP:** an `import_svg` tool, or the shared sketch-import tool with format svg (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Not in scope (later)

- Text to outlines (fonts), embedded images, and CSS stylesheets.

## Done means

- A fixture SVG set (a rectangle with a hole, Bézier and arc shapes, a nested group with transforms, mm and in documents, and one file without a physical size) imports to the expected sketch chains. The tests pin the chain count, closure, nesting and size within tolerance.
- A 2D Contour on an imported SVG posts. A golden is pinned for one plasma or waterjet-style profile.
- Malformed fixtures are refused by name and never panic. The importer fuzz test covers the SVG reader.
- The user guide import page (and #1525's waterjet notes) lists SVG.

Related: #1525 (waterjet research), #1452 (DXF umbrella), #1860-#1870 (DXF chain).

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860.

## Goal
Extend the `crates/geometry/src/dxf/` reader from #1860 to parse `SPLINE`, `ELLIPSE`, and bounded `BLOCK`/`INSERT` entities cleanly.

## Scope
- Parse `ELLIPSE` (center, major endpoint, axis ratio, start/end parameters, extrusion vector check) from Autodesk's published DXF Reference. Return exact `Circle`/`Arc` primitives when the axis ratio equals `1.0` within tolerance, and flatten non-circular ellipses adaptively within a caller chord tolerance in millimeters.
- Parse `SPLINE` (degree, flags, knot vector, control points, fit points, rational weights). Evaluate rational and non-rational B-splines via de Boor's algorithm and subdivide adaptively so chord deviation stays within the caller tolerance. Recover circular arcs when the spline matches a circle within tolerance. Reject malformed knot counts, negative weights, or non-finite control points by name.
- Pass the flattening chord tolerance through `ImportDxf` (#1862) and record it on import metadata.
- Parse `BLOCKS` definitions and expand `INSERT` references (translation, rotation, uniform X/Y scale, row/column array grids, and `0`-layer inheritance per DXF rules).
- Enforce strict recursion depth, total expanded entity count, and cycle detection caps against block bombs. Refuse cyclic references, external references (`XREF`), non-uniform X/Y shear scaling, or tilted OCS extrusions by block/entity name.

## Done means
Dense point sampling proves flattened `SPLINE` and `ELLIPSE` polylines stay within the stated tolerance in millimeters; circular splines and ellipses keep exact `Arc`/`Circle` segments; `INSERT` expands uniform blocks (and nested blocks within limits) accurately; cyclic blocks, sheared inserts, xrefs, and malformed splines return named errors with passing fuzz tests.

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

body:
**Bump egui, egui-winit and egui-wgpu from 0.36.2 to 0.37** (and wgpu to the matching version), so CamCraft's UI can share SolidCraft's UI crates.

**Why:** SolidCraft (tangency-labs/solidcraft, 0.40.0-rc) builds on `egui 0.37`, `eframe 0.37`, `egui-wgpu 0.37` (vendored) and `wgpu 30`. CamCraft pins `=0.36.2`. Two egui versions in one binary can't share types, so no SolidCraft crate (`solidcraft-theme`, `solidcraft-color` or the coming `solidcraft-ui-kit`) can be pinned until CamCraft is on 0.37. This is a prerequisite of #655.

**Done means:** the workspace builds on egui 0.37 with clippy clean. The ui suites and the structural tests (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs`) pass, and any API break is fixed in place. Snapshot PNGs aren't refreshed here; the cut does that (AGENTS.md). The `gpu_select` / `gpu_init` paths are re-checked on macOS Metal.

Part of #655
